entities.name: Exodus
entities.description:
The Exodus was a pivotal event in the history of the Brotherhood of Steel.

Four days after the onset of the Great War, Captain Roger Maxson led his rogue troops and their families from the Mariposa Military Base to Lost Hills, a journey which took them south-east.

The Exodus was described as a trying time and the group was attacked many times by marauders along the way, leading to some casualties. Additionally, the group split into two when Sergeant Dennis Allen wished to excavate the Glow, against Maxson's wishes. Allen's side robbed Maxson's side of their weapons and Maxson's side did not find out what happened to Allen's group after.

When Maxson's group arrived at the Lost Hills bunker, Maxson declared it their new home.
entities.short_description: The Exodus was a pivotal event in the history of the Brotherhood of Steel.

entities.name: Grand Canyon Brotherhood of Steel
entities.description:
The Grand Canyon Brotherhood of Steel is a chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel located near the Grand Canyon in Arizona in 2296.

Nothing is known about the Grand Canyon Brotherhood's scope or operations outside of having access to at least one Prydwen-class airship for transport. They became subordinate to the Commonwealth chapter sometime after the latter's formation and supposedly have been granted considerable autonomy in their operations by the dominant chapter. As of July 2296, its incumbent elder is an unnamed man.

The Grand Canyon Brotherhood became infamous among other chapters for an incident in which a male squire was caught having sex with a robot, which they have in turn argued was "well within his rights."

In 2296, the sitting elder of the chapter was invited to Area 51 by Elder Cleric Quintus of the Knights of San Fernando to discuss plans for a rebellion against the Commonwealth. Initially skeptical, the Grand Canyon elder wanted Quintus to handle the situation on his own, stating that his chapter enjoyed the autonomy granted by the Commonwealth. However, he accepted Quintus's offer to join forces with him and the Yosemite and Coronado chapters when he learned that the San Fernando chapter was capable of producing fusion cores on an industrial scale using the cold fusion diode, sufficient for a successful war against the Commonwealth. However, the arrival of Paladin Harkness from the Commonwealth complicated matters.

entities.name: Holotag
entities.description:
Holotags or dog tags are a form of identification device used by military personnel.

These tags (along with normal metal tags) were used by the United States Armed Forces and are used by the New California Republic Army, the Brotherhood of Steel, and the Enclave to store identification information and basic medical information for their personnel.

Holotags are small and durable tags used to identify their wearer in case of their death. They are not intrinsically valuable, but are used to track casualties by their issuer. They can also act as a data recorder for a suit of power armor, providing the issuer a record of the deeds of their fallen wearer. In some cases, information such as the soldier's full name, signature, identification number, blood type, security clearance, expiration date, base of operations, and a slogan You think you can take me? You go right ahead are displayed below a barcode. Other tags contain name and address only.

Holotags are mentioned in the Fallout: The Roleplaying Game rule book.

entities.name: Initiates
entities.description:
Initiates are trainee members in the Brotherhood of Steel. At times, chapters have used different ranks to refer to this class: in the Brotherhood's early years, its founding chapter and the Appalachian chapter labeled all trainees as squires, while in the late 23rd century, the Knights of San Fernando labeled all trainees as aspirants.

In general, initiates are the lowest ranking formal members of the Brotherhood, who are still receiving training and education for specialization into the higher orders of the Brotherhood, primarily those of the knights (soldiers) and scribes (researchers and engineers). Where applicable, they may also join other orders such as the lancers (pilots). Once their training as initiate is completed, they will advance into these higher orders. Beyond this, the specific practices around the rank have varied between Brotherhood of Steel chapters and over time.

In the foundational years of the Brotherhood, all trainees were instead called squires, regardless of age; the title was apparently reformed due to some adult trainees complaining about being given a title traditionally referring to children. With regards to recruitment, by 2277, the Capital Wasteland chapter was using squire as a rank for children born into the Brotherhood, with initiates instead being older, combat-ready recruits. By 2296, the Knights of San Fernando were using a wholly different system where recruits of any age were called aspirants, with squire being the next rank for aspirants on the soldier track (reversing the hierarchy of the Commonwealth chapter as of 2287, where aspirant was instead the next rank for initiates on the soldier track).

Methods of training and assignment have also differed between chapters. Some chapters use a system where initiates are mentored by specific higher-ranked members, who may have also sponsored their recruitment, whereas other chapters have used more communal training and education cohorts. Chapters may also mix these methods.

entities.name: Knights
entities.description:
Knights are a caste in the Brotherhood of Steel.

Knights are members of the Brotherhood that completed the training necessary to serve as technicians, engineers and soldiers if the need arises. They are competent fighters and excel in applied sciences, a complicated term for manufacturing weapons and ammunition, and maintaining the ever-expanding stock of combat technology in the Brotherhood's bunkers. During wartime, knights fill the role of infantry, security, military police, recruit instructors and aircrew operating airborne weapons systems.

After years of service and experience (or showing exceptional talent in combat), the best knights are promoted to paladins, the pinnacle of the Brotherhood military.

In the hierarchy of rogue chapters, such as in Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel and the Eastern Brotherhood of Steel, knights are strictly combat personnel, with their non-combat duties folded under the scribes' supervision.
entities.short_description: Knights are a caste in the Brotherhood of Steel.

entities.name: Knights of San Fernando
entities.description:
The Knights of San Fernando, also called the Knights of the San Fernando, are a chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel, active on the West Coast in 2296. Led by Elder Cleric Quintus, the chapter emphasizes the Brotherhood's quasi-religious beliefs and aesthetics with a strong presence of clerics in their ranks and adhere zealously to Brotherhood dogma to enact change in the wasteland. They appear in season 1 and season 2 of the Fallout TV series.

By 2296, the Knights of San Fernando have a significant presence on the West Coast, making their base at a pre-War airfield in the eponymous region of San Fernando.

By that year, the chapter's leadership is held by Elder Cleric Quintus, who is also assisted by various clerics and support personnel, such as Cleric Felix and Petty Officer Shortsight. Quintus believes the present-day Brotherhood has stagnated and lost its way, with his personal philosophy being that power is taken rather than given. Through his command of the San Fernando chapter, he plans to reform the organization and create a new Brotherhood as the dominant power in the wasteland, as it once was decades prior.

Circa 2283, Quintus, at the time a knight in T-60 power armor, was operating close to the NCR capital of Shady Sands when it was destroyed by a nuclear detonation orchestrated by Hank MacLean. Investigating the city ruins, he discovered a survivor: a boy placed inside a milk vending machine by his parents before the blast. The orphaned child came to admire and idolize the knight for their actions in finding and saving him. Quintus brought the boy back with him and later adopted him into the San Fernando chapter, given the name "Maximus" as an aspirant.

entities.description:
Lancers are members of the Brotherhood tasked with the maintenance and operation of its flying vehicles. The class was formed in the wake of the purifier conflict, as the Brotherhood gained access to large numbers of Vertibirds. By 2287, lancers operate both Vertibirds and The Prydwen, an airship built and maintained by the Brotherhood by Elder Arthur Maxson and Lancer Captain Kells, as it continues to serve the Brotherhood's goals.

entities.name: Paladins
entities.description:
Paladins are a caste in the Brotherhood of Steel.

Paladins are the protectors of the Brotherhood and their elite fighting force. Each is a highly trained combat veteran with high tech equipment at their disposal. They are responsible for maintaining security, from enemies both within and outside of the organization. The ranks of the paladins are reinforced through promoting veteran knights of exceptional combat aptitude. It is generally impossible to become a paladin any other way.

The head paladin is the overall commander of the paladins, responsible for implementing the elder's combat plans, enforcing Brotherhood laws and discipline on top of overseeing the overall training regime. They are a veteran, a talented soldier and are required to periodically convene with other caste heads and the elders.

Star paladins are only answerable to their elder and are given a wide authority to do what they see fit to accomplish their objectives.

entities.name: Brotherhood of Steel hierarchy
entities.description:
The Brotherhood of Steel relies on a strict hierarchy, where orders flow through the ranks and are carried out without hesitation. For a breakdown of the ranks themselves, see Brotherhood of Steel ranks.

Members of the Brotherhood are divided into distinct castes, each with a function of their own. The actual organization of the classes themselves and the ranks varies to some extent, typically by geographic region. Most follow the original regime for ranking. The Chain that Binds doctrine is traditionally intended to ensure obedience and conformity among the members of the Brotherhood, maximizing the efficiency of the Brotherhood as a war machine.

All members are subject to the same body of laws, at least in theory. Even elders may be dismissed for violating the Brotherhood's charter or laws, such as destroying technological devices without due cause, violating the Chain that Binds, or murdering a fellow member. Due to the requirement for elders to set an example, elders may also be stripped of their position if allowing them to retain it would compromise the morale or integrity of a given chapter.

In practice, the law is selective; for example, High Elder John Maxson could issue direct orders to the Vault Dweller, an initiate, without consequences. Elder McNamara's violation of the Chain that Binds have also gone unnoticed, due to chapter ignorance of large parts of the doctrine.

entities.name: Schism
entities.description:
A schism occurred within the Brotherhood of Steel in the Capital Wasteland from 2276 until 2283. Following a drastic shift in mission profile by Elder Lyons, a sizable group of Brotherhood loyalists broke off from the rogue Lyons' Brotherhood, forming their own sub-faction: the Brotherhood Outcasts.

In 2254, the Brotherhood's elder council, based in the Lost Hills bunker in New California, decided to send a expedition to the East Coast. The expedition's primary objective was to recover any and all advanced or vital technology from East Coast cities and bases. Secondly, they were to attempt to make contact with the "Eastern Brotherhood" that had fallen out of contact some time ago. The contingent was placed under the command of Star Paladin Owyn Lyons, accompanied by head technological advisor Senior Scribe Reginald Rothchild, as well as several veteran members of the Brotherhood, including paladins Henry Casdin and Tristan.

After traveling across the continent, the expedition had little success in contacting the Eastern Brotherhood. In 2255, Lyons' group arrived in the Capital Wasteland, establishing a base of operations within the Pentagon in the first few months. Though the Pentagon was partially destroyed, its sublevels remained, for the most part, intact, and its surviving stockpiles contained undisturbed pre-war technology and weaponry to sustain their operations. Their most significant find was Liberty Prime, an unfinished pre-War prototype large-scale combat robot. Following the discovery of Liberty Prime, Star Paladin Lyons received a new directive from his superiors in Lost Hills to establish a permanent Brotherhood presence in the Capital Wasteland, and continue the search for any other advanced technology hidden in the former capital's ruins. This expedition became the permanent Capital Wasteland chapter of the Brotherhood, led by the newly-promoted Elder Lyons.

After entering the region, the Brotherhood started to notice the large presence of super mutants, which deeply disturbed them. They quickly realized that these were a new breed of super mutant, not part of the ones who had fled east following the defeat of the Master's Army in 2161, and that they posed a dire threat to the region and its inhabitants. As such, around 2257, the Capital Wasteland chapter under Lyons launched a eradication campaign against the mutants. This was conducted with the goal of protecting civilians, but also to find and eliminate the source of the mutants.

entities.name: Scribes
entities.description:
Scribes are a caste in the Brotherhood of Steel. They are tasked with creating and keeping records of the technology recovered and used by the Brotherhood and experimenting with new weapons and other useful devices to be used in the field by the knights and paladins. Scribes rarely leave the safety of the Brotherhood bunkers, but they are sometimes called into the field to examine a piece of technology or perform a task beyond the skills of the Brotherhood soldiers. The attitude of many scribes in the Brotherhood can be described as techno-centric. While a great number study history and cultures, the majority of scribes focus their studies on subjects related to the acquisition, repair or creation of technology.

Scribes rarely leave the safety of the Brotherhood bunkers, but they are sometimes called into the field to examine a piece of technology or perform a task beyond the skills of the Brotherhood soldiers. The attitude of many scribes in the Brotherhood can be described as techno-centric. While a great number study history and cultures, the majority of scribes focus their studies on subjects related to the acquisition, repair, or creation of technology. Scribes are also assigned to educate young Brotherhood of Steel members. Their teachings involve the principles of science, including nuclear fusion, chemistry, and combat tactics.

There are three major scribe orders; each order is headed by a high scribe (proctor), designated by the head scribe.

The head scribe is the leader of the scribe class, responsible for its members, projects, asset assignment and high level command. The head scribe also chooses the high scribes or proctors of each order and must also oversee the projects each order is working on. In general, the head scribe is a highly intelligent person who has mastered the orders of the Sword, Shield and Quill, and may also take on a project of their own interest, as Head Scribe Rothchild did with the Liberty Prime Project. The head scribe is one of the people who must attend the meetings with the high elder, Elder Council, generals, head paladin and head knight. The head scribe reports only to the high elder and Elder Council.

entities.name: Steel Plague
entities.description:
The Steel Plague is the name given to a proposed evolution of the Lost Hills chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel .

The phenomenon of the "Steel Plague" was described as the Brotherhood fallen to extremism as a techno-religious dictatorship that would have formed in New California following the premature death of Rhombus and his successor taking power, where their increased fanaticism would have led to the destruction of the infant New California Republic around the 2180s, beginning another "Dark Age" for humanity that would have lasted centuries more.

The Steel Plague is only mentioned in the game's endings if the player character kills Rhombus in the game, preventing his ascension to the position of high elder and resulting in new leadership. The events of and have demonstrated that Rhombus' death and the subsequent development of the Steel Plague did not occur and are most likely non-canon. While the West Coast Brotherhood is demonstrated to have become more reactionary over time and ultimately come to war with the NCR, their ideology has seemingly remained largely moderate, with the term "Steel Plague" never appearing in any other Fallout media.

entities.name: Virtual reality pod
entities.description:
Virtual reality pods are large ovoid computer interface devices that process a virtual reality directly with its users mind.

The programming used in the different models varies by the intended purpose of the simulation.

An ovoid pod that contains a single chair inside. The user interface can be two high-resolution displays equipped with coils situated immediately in front of the user's face, or a worn neural interface suit depending on the model. The back and base of the chair contain all the hardware necessary to process the user's input into the simulation. The actual simulation runs through a processing center the pod is connected to. They have their built-in security protocols which are supposed to prevent harm from coming to the user in effect of injury or death within the simulation. If they are disabled death inside a simulation will be processed as having a cardiac arrest.

entities.description:
The Yosemite Brotherhood of Steel is a chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel located in Yosemite.

Nothing is known about the Yosemite Brotherhood's scope or operations outside of having access to at least one Prydwen-class airship for transport. They became subordinate to the Commonwealth chapter sometime after the latter's formation. As of July 2296, its incumbent elder is a woman named McRae.

According to Elder McRae, the Yosemite chapter does not follow the techno-religious practices observed in some chapters like the Knights of San Fernando. However, they may hold the Codex in particularly high regard, as McRae frequently cites it. Despite this cultural friction, the San Fernando and Yosemite chapters maintained close ties to the point they were considered allies by the former's leader, Elder Cleric Quintus.

In 2296, Elder McRae was invited to travel to Area 51 in the Mojave Wasteland by Elder Cleric Quintus of the Knights of San Fernando, along with the elders of the Grand Canyon and Coronado chapters. The meeting's goal was to discuss plans for an alliance against the Commonwealth Brotherhood with the aim of shifting power within the wider Brotherhood back to the West Coast.

entities.name: Religion
entities.description:
In the centuries following the Great War, some major pre-War religions and belief systems split into new delineations, while others continue to march along as they had for centuries prior. This is the case with Christianity and Mormonism, as various Christian and Mormon denominations and settlements exist, such as Catholicism and Protestantism. Although in the case of Mormonism which denominations did and didn’t survive is less certain. Christian organizations such as the Abbey of the Road send missionaries to preach the faith while scavenging holy sites for religious relics for restoration. The Catholics of Saint Monica's Church espouse a post-War version of the real-world story of Saint Monica, in which Monica is a ghoul. The followers of Dharma were originally from Hindu, Buddhist, and Sikh backgrounds, and include the founders of Shady Sands. Pre-War religious cults survived, and even thrived, in the absence of any kind of pushback from law enforcement or competing cultural institutions. These include the Hubologists, the Cult of the Mothman, and those who attempt to commune with Ug-Qualtoth.

However, in the wake of nuclear devastation, many new cults were established with a variety of belief systems. Some were developed over time from mythologized retellings of real events, such as the "Father in the Caves," the Sorrows deity inspired by Randall Clark's interactions with the fledgling tribe upon their arrival in Zion Canyon. Many small cults revere the spirits of plants and animals, such as the Vipers, or the tribe at Brahmin Wood. The Treeminders worship a captive "god," Harold the tree-mutant, despite his protests. Not all cults were created altruistically, such as the Renewal Cult, which was created wholly by a megalomaniacal mutant rat to take over the world.

The Children of the Cathedral are another doomsday cult, who serve the Master as a façade for his plan to use the FEV to unite humanity as supposedly perfect mutants. They originally served some kind of Dark God under the guidance of Morpheus, until the Master found them. He demanded their allegiance as spies, and their leader accepted. Some mutants still serve the lost cause of Unity. Others have found new spiritual callings, such as the wandering nightkin tribe who worship a brahmin skull they call Antler.

Ghouls have been known to form their own cults, especially those cast out from other societies. The Bright Brotherhood sought transcendence by escaping Earth on rocket ships. In the ruins of Kansas City, the ghoulified followers of Plutonius worship a nuclear warhead.

entities.name: Amish
entities.description:
The Amish are a pre-War Anabaptist Christian group well known for shunning most forms of modern technology. The group have their roots in European immigrants who formed religious communities in the United States of America in the 1700s.

To date in the series, at least one Amish community is known to have survived the aftermath of the Great War. At some point prior to 2103, Caleb Fisher, born and raised Amish, left the group while undertaking Rumspringa, a rite of passage in which young Amish members are allowed to leave their community for a short time to see the outside world. Leading up to his own departure, Fisher had become disillusioned with his peers after realizing some of them found satisfaction and validation in their way of life after the rest of the world was scorched by nuclear fire in 2077. Once the time came, he abandoned his family and friends and never returned.

In 2296, upon being released from his imprisonment by Honcho, Biggie, and Slim, the Ghoul remarks sarcastically about the situation seeming like "an Amish production of The Count of Monte Cristo."

entities.name: Apostles of the Eternal Light
entities.description:
The Apostles of the Eternal Light or Children of Light is a religious order who worship ghouls, founded by Mother Curie III. She departed from the Church of the Children of Atom congregation at Megaton, purportedly having experienced a vision from Atom which led her to reject Confessor Cromwell's gospel.

Less than two weeks after the activation of Project Purity in 2277 or 2278, the cult became known when they distributed holy water pamphlets in Megaton. Practicing out of their recently constructed monastery in Springvale, this evangelical off-shoot's main tenets are arguably heretical to the cult.

While meditating by wandering through in Springvale in a trance, Curie was approached by four members of Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel on their water delivery run to Megaton. When they found her there, she told them where she was from, and they told her to share the water with her people. In her religious stupor, she took this to be a vision from Atom himself. That four armored angels of war appeared, to give her the barrels of Aqua Pura and "bless" it with radiation to spread the cult's message of "enlightenment" to everyone. She and Brother Gerard would leave Confessor Cromwell's flock, no longer believing in the "Great Division," (seeing this belief as misguided and the C-23 Megaton nuclear weapon as a "great symbol" of Atom) to found a new order of the cult in Springvale, the Apostles of the Eternal Light. They constructed their monastery in the ruins of a home, adding exterior walls in front and installing a tabernacle. From the podium the radiation devices are activated on the pulpit, between which a bathtub rests. The actual order resides in the basement.

Their small but growing order seeks to tend to the ill through their brainwashing When consumed by hapless and unknowing wastelanders, They are used to religious persecution and they refuse to answer violence with violence, to a point. They even supply generous innocents like Rosa Meitner with excess supply, encouraging them to share the tainted water with any thirsty travelers they might encounter.

entities.name: Bright Brotherhood
entities.description:
The Bright Brotherhood is a religious cult in the Mojave Wasteland in 2281, based in the REPCONN test site west of Novac.

A strange cult of ghouls, and a single human fully believing himself to be a ghoul, the Bright Brotherhood is led by a charismatic and prophetic glowing one named Jason Bright. He never turned feral, and has instead built up a small following of like-minded ghouls, clad in the vestments and in the final stages of preparation for their "Great Journey" to the "Far Beyond:" a radioactive promised land glimpsed in visions by Bright that is the cult's ultimate goal and destination.

The Bright Brotherhood existed fully since before 2279, but it is unknown when the cult formed or where it started. The reasons can be surmised easily from the purpose of their "Great Journey," however, simple protection from the wasteland and bigoted humanity. Most of the Brotherhood's doctrines stem from visions that Jason Bright claims to experience, given to him by "the creator." He is amenable to skeptics who question or try to caution against his goals, but he considers the creator's will as shown by his visions to be the ultimate authority, and does not seek to actively convert skeptics like the Courier or Harland.

Around 2279, Chris Haversam came to the REPCONN test site believing he was a ghoul. Thus, this makes him the only human follower, although he was not allowed on the ship for the "Great Journey," which Bright says is the will of the creator. Jason also believes that it is no coincidence that two humans were instrumental to the success of the Great Journey, as it was the will of the creator and it is his blessing. He believes that the creator sent the Courier and Chris to expiate the sins of the bigoted humans. For helping the Brotherhood in making the Great Journey possible, they made Haversam a saint of the Brotherhood.

entities.name: Buddhism
entities.description:
Buddhism is a Dharmatic (i.e. philosophical) religion which is known to survive after the Great War amongst the Shi of San Francisco.

Buddhism is based on the beliefs and spiritual teachings of Gautama Buddha (also known as "the Buddha"), which focus on how one may achieve enlightenment (Nirvana) through practicing the Noble Eightfold Path. In traditional Buddhism, the Buddha is venerated more as a teacher than a deity. However, the invocation of the Buddha by the Shi's palace guards in death threats suggests that they consider the Buddha to be more directly involved in the judgement of the soul, presumably to determine if one is worthy of enlightenment.

Additionally, Zen Buddhism survives in the Capital Wasteland with a super mutant named Uncle Leo who emphasizes pacifism and altruism to everyone he meets. Meanwhile, Buddha is also remembered as a savior figure similarly to Jesus Christ.

Karma is a part of Buddhism that is the measurement of one's actions and intentions and determines if one can reach samsara. In most Fallout games, karma is a quantifiable metric that equates if the player character is good, neutral, or evil.

entities.name: Christianity
entities.description:
Christianity is a pre-War religion based on the life and teachings of Jesus Christ. The Fallout series depicts or mentions several branches of Christianity, including Catholicism, Protestantism, Pentecostalism, Anabaptist sects like the Amish and other derived religious denominations like Mormonism.

Christianity continues to be practiced in the post-War era on the North American continent. The ruins of churches can be found across the wasteland, while new Christian-derived groups have also been founded after the war, including Saint Monica's Church in Rivet City, and the Abbey of the Road, a Christian monastery said to be somewhere west of the Commonwealth. The settlement of New Canaan was founded by Mormon survivors in the city of Ogden, Utah, with missionaries continuing to travel and spread their faith to other wasteland inhabitants, such as the tribes of Zion Canyon, well into the 23rd century.

entities.name: Church of Harold
entities.description:
The Church of Harold is a cult formed around the worship of an FEV mutant called Harold. It is active on the West Coast.

The Church of Harold was founded by FEV mutants Blahblahwanna Rubra and Yaddayadda Glutinos (pre-FEV Bill Smith and Rex Rong) soon after an event simply referred to as the Great Shaking. Rubra and Glutinos' encounter with Harold, or tales of his influence over events in the wasteland, inspired them to create a religious organization. The Church was set up for the "lost", those lacking hope and feeling unfulfilled by life's "hints" for a satisfactory solution, and is open to all, including Numens as well as Oldmens, the latter so allowed out of Harold's respect for certain post-War individuals providing hope for the race.

It places no limits on the expectations of its followers, but it promises nothing and does not guarantee answers, however claims it will back up what it does proclaim. Despite its generic, almost vague, foundation, its aim remains hopeful; Our mission, stemming from the Union of Plant and Numen, is to Rebuild the world, one Twig at a time... ...All may know the peace that comes from following the Path of Harold. The Way is the Way.

Being part the Church entails adopting its customs. The Wearing of the Green is a simple symbol of faith representing Harold's tree, Bob, it requires wearing a plant on the head. More devout followers may undergo trephination (cutting a circular hole in the skull) followed by the nurturing of a tree in the hole, this is the final step towards becoming a "Vessel".

entities.description:
The Church of the Lost is a ghoul religion in the city of Los.

The majority of the city's population are members of this cult, dedicated to guarding the secret vault from the outside world and to eradicate all humans and super mutants that happen across their holy ground. Their leader and spiritual guide is Blake.

The Church of the Lost is indeed a powerful force. It is said that Blake rejects technology; despite this, the ghouls have access to some advanced weaponry, such as laser weaponry, and they use glowing one comrades, poison dogs, and even suicide bombers to fight their enemies.

The Church of the Lost consists not only of pre-War ghouls, but also ghouls who were turned after the war. Some of the members, including Blake himself, have been ghouls for little over 20 years, created by the explosion in the secret Vault from which they originally came.

entities.name: Cult of the Mothman
entities.description:
The Cult of the Mothman (or simply the Mothman Cult) is a religious movement in the region of Appalachia based in the exaltation of the Truth of the Mothman, though the term is often used by outsiders to refer to the largest faction, the Followers of the Winged One. Prior to the Great War, the faithful congregated in a small makeshift church under the Mothman Museum in Point Pleasant.

Mere days before the bombs fell, Brother Charles experienced a vision, which prompted the cultists to seek shelter in the faraway Lucky Hole Mine. Following the War, mutant creatures resembling the legendary Mothman were seen across Appalachia, and the cultists eventually emerged from the mine to engage with them in various ways.

The religion split into two major sects, which are bitterly at war;

Prior to the Great War, the Mothman was a mythical creature in Appalachian folklore, considered a "cryptid" in pop culture. Described as a terrifying half-man, half-moth hybrid, it was believed to haunt the area around Point Pleasant. entities.name: Dharma
entities.description:
Dharma is a religious entity mentioned in Fallout.

According to Aradesh, Dharma was a "great, religious man." Some residents of Shady Sands in 2161 claim to be followers of Dharma, including Aradesh, Agatha, Seth, and Katrina. Several sayings are attributed to him as listed below. However, it is unclear if Dharma was a pre-War historical figure, a post-War philosopher, or a mythical figure.

The following quotes are said by Aradesh and Agatha in interactions but are attributed to Dharma:

Dharma is an important religious concept in many Indian religions, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism, among others. While not easily translated into English, it can generally be summarized as actions or behaviors that are righteous, moral, or otherwise keeping with the natural order of the universe.

entities.name: Goddess of the Sea
entities.description:
The Goddess of the Sea is a minor deity worshipped by fishing tribes inhabiting the Pacific Coast in northern New California.

A type of animistic religion, the Goddess of the Sea is believed to inhabit the waters of the Pacific Ocean, watching the coastal tribes. The tribes perform a variety of rituals depending on the time of the year to appease the goddess. For example, before a large storm they hurl spears into the sea to demonstrate their bravery against the elements, and if the goddess judges them worthy, she returns mutfruit with the tide. When the season of storms begins, the tribes throw broc flowers into the sea with the tide, with xander root returned after the goddess "works her magic."

Xander root is part of a tribute given to the goddess each year, once again thrown into the sea. If the goddess deems them worthy, she turns the xander into broc flower. Another tribute is given to her after a bountiful harvest, in order to convince her to watch over and protect the tribes. The piety they demonstrate is demonstrated every year by returning spears with the tide.

The tribes freely trade the gifts of the goddess with outsiders, though only those capable of rational conversations. Those who cannot are directed towards the sea, to meet the goddess personally. When departing, the tribesmen customarily wish the blessing of the goddess on visitors.

entities.name: Hubology
entities.description:
The Church of Hubology is a cult founded in the pre-War United States. It maintains a major presence in San Francisco around 2241 and has a smaller outpost at Nuka-World by 2287. Its followers are known as Hubologists.

Hubology was founded by Dick Hubbell before the Great War. Disillusioned with contemporary government, religion, and medicine, and inspired by contemporary music and alleged encounters with extraterrestrial beings, Hubbell created the religion to help humanity understand existence through the "Great Wheel of Life."

To his followers, he is known as "The Hub," entrusted by the Star Father with the secrets to reaching the planet Quetzal. He also invented the Zeta ray emitter used in "alignment" rituals to cleanse neurodynes.

Pre-War mainstream society and media labeled the movement pseudoscience. After facing persecution, Hubologists infiltrated opposing organizations and produced media to spread their message. The cult's survival of the Great War (referred to internally as the "Great Deluge") is seen by its followers as proof of the Great Wheel's favor. All of Hubbell's writings, no matter how mundane, are considered holy texts.

entities.name: Mars
entities.description:
Mars is the ancient Roman god of war and deity who is worshipped by members of Caesar's Legion.

The worship of Mars is mentioned throughout the Legion. Legate Lanius, commander of the Legion army, informs the Courier that the Son of Mars granted him his name, and that he is whom he serves. If the Courier chooses to align with the Legion, Lanius will leave them with parting words on their way to Hoover Dam, imploring them not to fail Mars or the Legion, as Mars' eyes are upon them. Caesar refers to himself as the "Son of Mars" and the belief system of which they follow claims that Mars cleansed the Earth with fire to facilitate Caesar's conquest of the Earth. Caesar, as the son of Mars, has his power often inflated and deified in the eyes of legionaries, who see Caesar as a supernatural entity who gives strength to those he favors.

Recently captured slaves are usually skeptical of that claim, but their children are taken by the Legion to be raised by priestesses to effectively indoctrinate them into the cult.

Believing that the weak and wicked are brought low, the son of Mars rules with the goal of delivering the wasteland from chaos and barbarism. The belief in justice as a driving force is echoed by Legion members in conversation, but not all live up to that standard. Ritual sacrifice is practiced by Legate Lanius, who sacrifices captured NCR troopers and slaves in the hopes of appeasing Mars to grant him victory in battle.

entities.name: Mechminster Abbey
entities.description:
Mechminster Abbey is a settlement introduced in Winter of Atom.

Despite its dilapidated state, the abandoned church still serves as a place of devotion, though its focus has shifted towards reverence for steel, fire, and all things mechanical. Mechminster Abbey, governed by the Sisters of the Forge, a dedicated group of female blacksmiths and mechanics adorned with c-wrench necklaces instead of rosaries, remains a beacon of hope. Uttering their prayers in hushed tones, "Where there is light, there is hope," the Sisters tirelessly stoke the forge, providing charitable aid to those fighting the noble battle in the Commonwealth. Firmly opposing the Last Son of Atom and his perilous doctrine, they commit themselves to guiding others away from his influence. Regrettably, the harsh winter conditions have caused a shift in their priorities. Scarce food supplies and a recent onslaught of frost feral ghouls have thrown Mechminster Abbey's defenses into disarray. With their pews filled and their coffers depleted, the Sisters find themselves in need, compelled to extend their reach and seek external assistance.

This small settlement has just 43 settlers, somewhat weak defenses, limited food supply, and a somewhat grim outlook on life.

The Sisters hold all Children of Atom to be heretics who offend their faith. Children of Atom characters are likely to be unwelcome in the Abbey.

entities.name: Pillars of the Community
entities.description:
The Pillars of the Community are a small cult based in the Charles View Amphitheater, operating in the Commonwealth in 2287.

Presenting themselves as a new movement that is quickly gaining traction in the Commonwealth, the Pillars of the Community seeks to gain new followers through the distribution of fliers to nearby settlements. Its missionaries promise those who join a "better life" and welcome all who come to the Charles View Amphitheater seeking the "truth" about the troubled world. A man named Brother Thomas leads the cult and personally sees all new initiates who are looking to become members. He sometimes pays a visit to settlements to spread the word about the Pillars, and encourages all new members to voluntarily give up all of their "worldly possessions" as a first step toward "salvation."

A trained eye can discover that the cult is in reality a cover for a scam operated by Thomas and his missionaries. The scammers use their fliers and message of false hope to lure unsuspecting wastelanders to the amphitheater, where Thomas can extort them for their possessions, threatening to kill them unless they hand over everything peacefully. In fact, locals are annoyed of hearing about the conman's "salvation racket," and Ham eventually had to throw Thomas out of the Third Rail in Goodneighbor because he was bothering customers. He has even caused trouble for the affluent Cabot family by kidnapping and holding their daughter Emogene after a "disagreement" over joining the Pillars of the Community in which she turned violent. Due to the effects of a mysterious serum she uses, it took the entire cult combined to get Emogene subdued and locked up. Eventually, the Cabots could send their new mercenary, the Sole Survivor, to find Emogene.

Upon approach, Brother Thomas, under the name of Brother Andrew, Brother Simon, Brother James or Brother Matthew, will initiate dialogue with the Sole Survivor. Whether the player character accepts to join or not, at the end of his dialogue he will ask the player character to follow him to his office. In his office, Brother Thomas will tell the Sole Survivor to give him all of their belongings, to which they can either give them to him or opt not to.

entities.name: Plutonius
entities.description:
Plutonius is a nuclear warhead worshiped as a god by a cult of ghouls in Kansas City in 2197. It was produced by Manhattan Projects Inc.

Before the Great War, Kansas City was a major nuclear launch site. After the city was hit by the bombs, the surviving silo staff were turned into ghouls, and formed a town called Gravestone in the ruins of the city. Only one nuclear bomb was left intact in the silos, and the ghouls took to worshiping it as a god, "Plutonius."

Plutonius was later taken by the Brotherhood of Steel, placed on nuke carrier, and used to crack open the entrance to Vault 0 in order to assault the Calculator.

The bomb's name is derived from the radioactive element Plutonium, one of the three primary isotopes utilized in nuclear fission.

entities.description:
The Renewal is a cult based in Gecko. Its symbol is an ankh, and its members wear talismans of ankh.

Renewal was founded by a mole rat who became sapient after an FEV dose. This rat settled in Gecko, named itself "The Brain" and began seeking to take over the world.

Brain sought to build an alliance between Gecko and Vault City based on power from Gecko being sent to Vault City in exchange for medical research on how to "restore" the ghouls to humanity. Brain was recruiting followers from ghouls and glowing ones living in Gecko, but could not talk to somebody in Vault City because of xenophobia.

The Chosen One can become a Renewal member and work towards completion of Brain's ideas. This includes fixing the reactor, optimizing it, and convincing McClure to accept an alliance between the two locations. However, a bug prevents play of an ending slide that reflects these choices.

entities.name: Saint Monica's Church
entities.description:
Saint Monica's Church is the local church of Rivet City, derived from Christianity. It is run by Father Clifford and his acolyte Diego in 2277.

What is known of the Church's theology is based on Catholicism, through the sermons of Father Clifford. As of 2277, the father's sermons center around a warped retelling of the story of Saint Monica, the patron saint of lost children, who is popular amongst Rivet City's faithful. In their version of the story, Monica is the miraculous daughter of two ghouls who is enslaved with her son Ehren; Ehren eventually turns into a slaver himself, but through constant faith and love Monica leads Ehren to repent for his ways. Other values Clifford espouses in his sermons are tolerance and acceptance, in response to the tensions between the city's Upper Deck and Hangar Deck denizens. Even though the church is empty every day but Sunday, Clifford will still preach to an empty house, as he believes that it is enough even if only God and Saint Monica hear his sermons. Although popular, his sermons are also repetitive, and many attendees (including Diego) struggle to stay awake during mass. Oblivious to this, he intends to make his next sermon on one of the seven deadly sins, though he hasn't decided which one.

That being said, Father Clifford's regular audience do appreciate him for his services, which help strengthen their faith and comfort them. especially Vera Weatherly, who even gives Father Clifford and Diego free meals as thanks. Meanwhile, Clifford also engages in outreach all across the city, encouraging more people to attend church and providing counseling and aid to those in need; as he says, all of Rivet City is his flock. and reduce Mister Lopez's suicidal tendencies. Others, like Ted Strayer and Doctor Preston, simply don't believe in the faith. The staff and patrons of the The Muddy Rudder, such as Belle Bonny, Trinnie, Brock, and Sister, are particularly hostile to Clifford, as they consider him to be an unwanted and overly moralizing intrusion upon their lives. Among their other community efforts, they regularly visit the Rivet City clinic to pray for Doctor Preston's patients.

Father Clifford took in Diego after the latter's father abandoned him in Rivet City, and the pair have become like father and son. Diego has since become the church's acolyte, assisting Clifford in his outreach, and studying to succeed him in the priesthood. However, Diego has recently become caught between his relationship to the church and his relationship with Angela Staley, who is in love with him. Father Clifford is well aware of these attempts, and has told Diego that Angela is his temptation before he can attain the priesthood. As so many of Clifford's hopes for the Church lie in Diego, especially because there is no else in line for the priesthood, he consider it devastating for Diego to leave. For his part, Diego has resisted all of Angela's advances so far. Should Father Clifford die, Diego will take his place as priest of the Church.

entities.name: The Enlightened
entities.description:
The Enlightened, or the Wise Mothman's Enlightened, are a religious faction who do not live in Appalachia, but travel there seasonally to hold a summoning ceremony. The group was formed when some members of the pre-War Cult of the Mothman rejected the post-War developments of the religion, and fled the state together. They have since come to exclusively revere the purple-eyed Wise Mothman, but do not worship him as a god. The Enlightened appear as the central faction in the seasonal public event The Mothman Equinox .

After an attempt by the Cult of the Mothman to summon their benefactor on October 22, 2077, it was proclaimed by an unknown preacher that the member known as Brother Charles had received a vision from the Mothman in the periphery of his senses, The Enlightened now believe Charles' revelations were the Whispers of the Wise Mothman, and recount the omen as a warning of "fire and flood."

Heeding this omen, the Cult of the Mothman crossed the state to the cliffs overlooking Watoga, to take shelter in the depths of Lucky Hole Mine. No contemporary evidence exists of who suggested this specific destination or why, but in modern times, the Enlightened claim it was Brother Charles who guided his brethren to the safety of the mine.

The Cult of the Mothman were not the first mysterious group to seek sanctuary here. No later than March 2061, an old woman (who seemed to be mentally unwell) The note His home seems to indicate that the post-War dwellers of the mine believe this event fulfilled a prophecy, which foretold that they would be denied entrance into their "new home" three times by the faithless, before "He would open the way."

entities.name: Treeminders
entities.description:
The Treeminders are a peaceful religious tribe that protects Oasis in the Capital Wasteland in 2277.

The Treeminders are an exclusive cult built around the worship of Harold, an FEV mutant that nurtured a tree that grew out of his head and eventually overwhelmed his body. He took root in the northern Capital Wasteland and was found by a wanderer in the late 2250s. This wanderer, later taking the name Birch, beheld the glory of Harold and knew other wanderers would seek to do the Great One harm. He founded the Treeminders, a group of pure-hearted individuals that would protect the Great One as his last line of defense. Once Harold took root, a verdant vale of growth spread from the tree, washing the barren hillside over with life and greenery, and enticing animal life to inhabit the area. The water in the area is still irradiated however, interpreted by Tree Father Birch as a way to be reminded of who they once were.

After Birch founded the Treeminders, others heard of an Oasis in the wasteland and made a pilgrimage to it, simply stumbled upon it in their aimless wandering or felt a calling from the Great One. Once there, they heeded the call of Birch to protect the Great One from the influences of the wasteland. Over time, the ranks of the Treeminders grew into a handful of people dedicated to keep the Great One from being exploited.

In 2277, a schism has divided the Treeminders into two camps. Tree Father Birch, among others, seek to keep Harold's influence in the secluded vale, fearing that opening it to the rest of the wasteland will mean its inevitable exploitation and destruction. As such, Birch desires that Harold's heart, found deep beneath his roots, be slathered with a harmless sap to curb his influence from spreading. Leaf Mother Laurel and others, however, wish to see Harold's influence spread across the wasteland and rebirth the world in his image. She feels Birch does not understand that Harold's growth is a miracle rather than a curse and benefits the entire wasteland. In opposition to Birch's plans, Laurel wishes to cover Harold's heart with a liniment that would accelerate Harold's growth and bring life to the wasteland in mere decades.

entities.name: Tribals
entities.description:
The Point Lookout tribals are a minor faction encountered .

Sometime prior to 2277, while wandering within a natural grotto, Jackson discovered a strange device and inadvertently activated it. The device was actually a projector, and Jackson believed that the hologram that emerged was the manifestation of a powerful spirit. In reality, this hologram was a broadcast of the disembodied brain of Professor Calvert, who had been in hiding around Point Lookout for decades since the Great War. Influenced by Calvert's manipulations, Jackson would return to the grotto more and more and commune with the "spirit," passing on the wisdom of the "Transcendent One" to the growing number of followers he had collected in his unnamed tribe.

The tribe began cultivating punga fruit and sold it to passers-by like Tobar, a ferryman who traveled along the East Coast in his vessel, the Duchess Gambit. The fruit's natural addictive properties drew a steady stream of addicts in addition to entrepreneurs, who later would wind up inducted into the tribe.

However, despite the tribe's zealotry and obedience towards him, Jackson's cult is the last thing Calvert wants. Living agents able to carry out his will would seem fortunate, but Calvert is left frustrated by Jackson's constant misinterpretations of the Professor's dictations, viewing them as religious instruction while unable to execute the simplest of demands, resulting in Calvert harboring a considerable amount of contempt for the "simpering spiritualist and his tribe of idiots" and an eagerness to replace Jackson with anyone of greater competency at the first chance.

entities.name: Tribals
entities.description:
A tribe is an ambiguous term, generally used to refer to stateless societies that emerged across the wasteland, characterized by the absence of formal government, a distinct cultural identity, and self-sufficiency. The term tribal is typically used as a pejorative noun by inhabitants of various non-tribal communities to describe someone as primitive, uncouth, and unsophisticated.

In a broad sense, every human society can be described as a tribe, a linked family of families, regardless of the place they inhabit or other circumstances.

Joshua Graham describes wasteland tribes as a connection of "families of families," where the family unit extends beyond blood relations and often encompasses the entire community. This results in much more close-knit communities than in other wasteland settlements, but also tends to make these tribes highly insular and wary of outsiders.

Tribals often possess a highly religious or mythologized view of the world, in contrast to more cynical or secular worldviews held by other wastelanders. As such, some tribes consider pre-War technology and structures taboo, preferring to live in isolated agrarian communities or as nomadic hunter-gatherers.

entities.name: 80s
entities.description:
The 80s are a mentioned-only faction . A tribe of raiders said to live in the northern areas of the former state of Utah, near the shores of the Great Salt Lake, they are a frequent and long-time enemy of the White Legs.

The 80s are known for their habit of raiding frontier towns for supplies and kidnapping people. They are rightly feared for their ability to cover large areas of land with very few men. Stella mentions that in the past, a group of the raiders abducted and killed two working girls from Caliente. After they were forced to give up their search, she says that if the 80s wanted her and her town members dead, they would have killed them, guessing that the raiders didn't think they were worth the trouble.

Despite not being involved in the War for Zion, the 80s' fate is indirectly tied to its outcome. If the White Legs are defeated by the Courier and Joshua Graham, but Salt-Upon-Wounds is left alive, the tribe's oldest enemy capitalizes on their fall from grace, scattering the tribe and eventually conquering the Great Salt Lake for themselves. Likewise, if Salt-Upon-Wounds is killed by the Courier in the Three Marys, the 80s go further and completely annihilate the White Legs to a man. In either case, their territorial expansion does not come without a price, as the remaining tribes of Zion eventually unite against the 80s and drive them away from Highway 50.

The 80s tribe first appeared in Joshua Sawyer's unofficial, personal Fallout role-playing game made in 2004. In it, they were described as "a gang of bandits that operate along the Northern California 80 Freeway, mostly in the region northeast of the lawless, uncontrolled city of Sacramento." Their insignia and typical outfits were also outlined, as well as their usage of motorcycles. The 80s were eventually incorporated into the series canon with Honest Hearts, albeit merely mentioned in the background.

entities.name: Blackfoot
entities.description:
The Blackfoot were a tribe that lived in the former state of Arizona and played a pivotal role in the history of Caesar's Legion as the first of the 86 tribes that constitute it.

At some point in 2247, Mormon missionary Joshua Graham, as well as two Followers of the Apocalypse - Bill Calhoun and Edward Sallow ventured into the Grand Canyon. Edward had been sent there to learn the dialects of the canyon tribes, with Calhoun sent to assist, and the pair met with Joshua along the way. Upon reaching their goal, they climbed down into the canyon and encountered the Blackfoot first. Graham was able to communicate with them, and the two groups at first had friendly relations. However, at one point the tribe became hostile for an unknown reason, capturing the three and holding them for ransom. Graham would come to blame himself, believing that he must have mistranslated something causing the Blackfoot to turn on them and decide that the outsiders wouldn't be leaving. At the time the tribe was at war with seven other tribes, a war they were inevitably going to lose. Unwilling to be destroyed along with them, and against the wishes of his companions, Sallow chose to use his knowledge to train the Blackfoot tribe in the art of warfare after witnessing their lack of knowledge firsthand. He showed them how to clean and maintain guns, operate with small unit tactics, create their own explosives and to strike at their weakest enemies first; divide et impera - divide and conquer (Latin). He quickly impressed them enough to the point where he was made their leader.

He soon introduced the concept of total war to the tribes around them - Sallow knew that though the tribes had always fought each other via occasional skirmishes, he considered them to only be "playing at war" having never seen warfare at its most destructive and barbaric. They defeated the weakest of their enemies first and enslaved many of the able-bodied survivors but Sallow ordered the rest, including women and children, killed and their remains piled high. When they confronted the next tribe, they brought an emissary back to view the carnage. The concept of total war was an entirely new, and terrifying, facet to his strategy that the Grand Canyon tribes had never confronted before, one that would form the core of the Legion's tactics and outlook.

entities.name: Mojave Boot-Riders
entities.description:
The Mojave Boot-Riders (simply referred to as the Boot Riders by members) were a nomadic tribe inhabiting the Mojave, before they settled in New Vegas and became the Chairmen.

One of the many nomadic tribes that formed out of the ruins of the Old World, the Boot-Riders roamed the Mojave. Their situation changed when they were approached by a securitron east of Vegas. The tribesmen destroyed it in a "minute flat." The following day, twenty securitrons approached them and they were forced to negotiate with Robert House. In return for shelter, food, and medical care, they would settle down, renovate the Tops, and work with Mr. House to establish the city of New Vegas. Most members of the tribe were against settling down, with one of the most vocal critics being Bingo, the chief at that time. Benny, on the other hand, saw it as an opportunity.

The disagreement over this issue eventually led to a confrontation between Benny and Bingo. The latter challenged Benny to a ritual knife fight over the leadership of the tribe. The fight went down three days after House had made his proposal. Benny's quick reflexes left him as the victor and new leader of the tribe. The tribe moved to Vegas and began renovating the Tops, bringing it back to life. As they worked, a number of House's securitrons dropped off boxes with suits, ties, and wingtip shoes, together with a message from their employer announcing they were the Chairmen now. The tribe was in an uproar over the new name, but Benny used his authority to force them to accept it. As he put it, it was "ciao to the old ways" and "time to swing in style."

The Ridgers were a tribe exterminated by Edward Sallow and the Blackfoots.

The Ridgers were the weakest among the seven tribes at war with the Blackfoot tribe when Edward Sallow was captured. After training the Blackfoot members in warfare, he led them against the Ridgers first. The tribe refused to surrender, so Edward ordered every man, woman, and child killed. He then led the Blackfoot against the Kaibabs, who likewise refused. In response, he took one of the Kaibab envoys back to the Ridgers' village to provide an example of what they were capable of. After this display, the Kaibabs joined the Blackfoot under Sallow's command, pushing forward to conquer other tribes.

entities.name: Twisted Hairs
entities.description:
The Twisted Hairs were a tribal group that lived in the former state of Arizona.

Once a powerful tribe that dominated their territory, the Twisted Hairs were named for the iconic and elaborate dreadlocks worn by their members. These braiding techniques were used by tribe members to document their personal histories, messages, and achievements through their hair for other tribe members to see, such as marriage, profession, and how many enemies they'd killed. These details were customary to the tribe; outsiders observing their braids would not necessarily see the information they carried unless made aware of it. The tribe's hairstyles also had other uses, such as providing material suitable for wrapping wounds to cut off venom, a technique they called the snakebite tourniquet.

The Twisted Hairs forged an alliance with Caesar in the early days of his Legion's rise to power, acting as scouts for Caesar's conquest of the tribes inhabiting the region. Once the Legion had secured victory against the other tribes with their help, Caesar and Vulpes Inculta met with the tribe at Dry Wells, where they "rewarded" the Twisted Hairs by breaking the alliance and betraying them, conquering and enslaving them as was and would be done to all the other tribes of Arizona. Their tribal identity was erased, and those that resisted were crucified along the sides of Interstate 40.

Ulysses was a former member of the Twisted Hairs, and he still wears the namesake hairstyle of the tribe even after being conscripted as a Legion frumentarius following their forced assimilation; whether he was allowed to keep his braids or he regrew them during his travels away from Caesar is unknown, since the Legion's assimilation tactics involves completely wiping out a tribe's identity and individuality. Even the name "Ulysses" is one he gave himself (in reference to Ulysses S. Grant), and he never reveals his tribal name, leaving it unclear if the Twisted Hairs had any special naming customs similar to other tribes like the Great Khans or the Dead Horses.

entities.name: State
entities.description:
A state of the United States was a pre-War geographic territory with established borders within the United States of America, formed into commonwealths, and then into the federal republic.

Though essentially defunct with the dissolution of the United States following the nuclear apocalypse, the names of the former American states are still used by the inhabitants of the wasteland and mentioned multiple times in the Fallout series.

Prior to the Great War, the United States of America was comprised of a total of 50 states. The states were created as a result of thirteen British colonies declaring independence in 1776. The ensuing American Revolutionary War secured the split, and the group of states adopted a constitution, joining the states together as a single republic.

Canada was annexed into the United States in the 2070s as a U.S. territory. Though some Americans referred to it as the "Big 51," alluding to it being seen by them as the official 51st state, this is not known to have formally occurred.

entities.name: Affordable Al's Discount Hospital
entities.description:
Affordable Al's Discount Hospital is a location .

A private pre-War hospital, the six-storey Affordable Al's was advertised as offering advantageous prices, including "revolutionary treatments" for the New Plague at low rates, lobotomies at half price, and comprehensive weight loss programs (on top of other hospital services, such as emergency rooms and surgery). After the Great War, the hospital was abandoned, with many patients left to die on the gurneys with no assistance.

Scavenged and damaged by centuries of neglect and the elements, it eventually became a nest for a swarm of radscorpions.

Lucy and the Ghoul, on their way to New Vegas, investigate the hospital when they hear a woman scream for help. Despite the Ghoul's insistence, she enters the hospital, with the Ghoul reluctantly following along with CX404. Exploring the derelict, skeleton-strewn building they locate the woman and a wounded man in the basement kitchen. While Lucy tends to the woman, the Ghoul kills the man after recognizing them both as respectively a Caesar's Legion slave and a legionary. The commotion attracts the attention of the radscorpions, leading to a fight in which both the woman and the Ghoul are struck and poisoned by the giant radscorpion. Lucy decides to treat the woman with her only stimpak, leaving the Ghoul to slowly regenerate under CX404's watch.

entities.name: Area 51
entities.description:
Pre-War, Area 51 was a military garrison for the United States Air Force. It housed research facilities studying captured alien technology, including a flying saucer. The vessel was later retaken by its alien crew, but ended up crashing somewhere within California where it remained well into the 23rd century by 2161. By late 2077, other artifacts stored in its warehouses included a preserved Zetan corpse; various pieces of alien technology including a shock baton, alien blaster, and UFO; a copy of the Constitution of the United States; an artifact resembling the Ark of the Covenant; a Terracotta Army soldier, a Holy Hand Grenade, a vintage red automobile; and various other statues and sculptures.

The facility's location within the deserts of the West Coast inspired military engineers to create an array of wind turbines around its perimeter, powered by a fusion generator, that could rapidly clear away large sand deposits in minutes (similar to the DERVISH camouflage system utilized by the bunkers of Hidden Valley). When not in use, the turbines themselves are housed within underground silos to preserve them.

After the nuclear apocalypse, a number of Zetan aliens that had been held captive within the facility escaped and retreated to Skull Canyon.

At some point, the rolling sands and desert winds of the wasteland buried much of the pre-War structures under an immense layer of sand, but the power control tower for the wind turbine array (housed in a fake playground rocket structure) was left exposed and accessible.

entities.name: Atomic Wrangler Casino
entities.description:
The Atomic Wrangler Bar & Casino, typically shortened to just the Atomic Wrangler, is an unmarked location within Freeside in the Mojave Wasteland . It also appears in season 2 of .

The Atomic Wrangler Bar & Casino was a pre-War nightclub located on Fremont Street in Las Vegas, Nevada, advertising itself as "the West's finest watering hole." In 2077, it played host to a meeting between Cooper Howard and Congresswoman Diane Welch, who arranged for Howard to secretly meet with the U.S. president in order to give him the cold fusion diode Howard had stolen from Vault-Tec.

By 2281, the Atomic Wrangler is the only active casino in the slum community of Freeside, also doubling as a flophouse, brothel, and prominent source of the chems craze in the area. Its owners and operators are the Garret twins, James and Francine, who keep a staff of armed thugs for protection and provide service even to members of the Van Graffs in the nearby Silver Rush and the Kings from the down-the-street King's School of Impersonation. Many caravaneers and poor (but not impoverished) NCR folks can also be found here when they lack deep enough pockets to make it to the Strip.

As of 2296, the Atomic Wrangler continues to operate in Freeside, though by then, the barkeep is a man named Shotgun Jeff and it is unclear whether the Garret twins are still involved with the establishment.

entities.name: BBQ Shack
entities.description:
Formerly a business establishment in the pre-War era in the former city of Santa Monica, California, sometime after the destruction of the NCR capital of Shady Sands in 2283, Sorrel Booker formed an organization of his own out of a self-righteous mission to restore order in Los Angeles, naming it the Govermint with himself as its president and claimed the old restaurant as their headquarters. From here, they conduct their operations including sending "sheriffs" to collect tribute paid to them by those they secure under their protection rackets including the organ-harvesters Huey and Squirrel out of a nearby Super Duper Mart outlet.

Booker's crew also seemingly maintains a small farm close to the building, raising hogs to slaughter for meat to feed themselves as well as utilizing the animals as low-tech body disposal if the need arises.

While the legitimacy of the Govermint's bounties is questionable, the BBQ Shack's wall features an assortment of bounty posters for valuable targets, with notable ones including Lee Moldaver, at least one super mutant, and a couple of ghouls by 2296.

After being picked up by sheriffs of the Govermint at the destroyed Super Duper Mart following the deaths of their clients Huey and Squirrel a short time prior, the Ghoul is brought to their HQ at the BBQ Shack and re-introduced to Govermint president Sorrel Booker, who recognizes the mutant bounty hunter from a past encounter and mentions his lifelong quest for "her," but is brushed off by the Ghoul who instead focuses on using a needle and thread to reattach the finger previously bitten off by Lucy MacLean.

entities.name: Brotherhood base
entities.description:
A remote pre-War airport on the West Coast, the facility was taken over by the Knights of San Fernando chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel sometime before 2296. It has since served a pivotal role in the Brotherhood's operations in and around New California, acting as a training camp for the Brotherhood's countless aspirants.

The area is introduced alongside the character of Maximus as other initiates are beating him by a set of bunker entrances before scattering. Many areas of the airbase are seen, including the runway, watchtower, barracks, and main hangars. Maximus is sentenced to latrine duty and exhibits extreme anger and frustration.

Later during an engineering lesson in a hangar, the class is interrupted, with the aspirants running outside to see the arrival of the Prydwen and a squad of knights from the Eastern Brotherhood in T-60 armor. Maximus and Dane later sneak off to get an up-close look at one of the suits being stored in the garage.

The base's layout includes extensive runways, hangars, barracks, and command facilities. Large swaths of tarmac allow Brotherhood Vertibirds to take off and land safely. A watchtower overlooks the runway and is also used by younger Brotherhood initiates to smoke. Initiates are seen clearing pathways, suggesting that the Brotherhood had recently taken the airbase, or are in the middle of restoring or expanding it. The base is also home to a large underground bunker complex, with at least nine separate partially submerged bunker entrances being visible adjacent to the airfield. Brotherhood of Steel members can be seen building what looks to be roadways between the bunkers and the rest of the base.

entities.name: Caesar's Legion camp
entities.description:
The Caesar's Legion camp is a location in the Mojave Wasteland in the Fallout TV series.

By 2296, the camp seems to be the central occupation of Caesar's Legion in the Mojave Wasteland while internally divided by a civil war between opposing factions of legionaries, led by two claimants to the throne that was left empty after the death of Edward Sallow sometime prior. Sallow's desiccated skeleton lies upon the dirt wall that marks the border between the two camps.

Following her capture by legionaries the night before, Lucy MacLean is brought into the camp, where she is exposed to the cruelty and violence inherent to the Legion. She is brought before the Lacerta Legate, who has the wounded woman Lucy helped beheaded for not returning to the camp with her legionary master. She is then led to meet one of the two Caesars and sees the legate without his helmet. Once Lucy learns her fate of being subjected to prima noctis, she speaks up in her own defense, including revealing her years of experience with "cousin stuff" and lack of virginity that astounds the legionaries.

The legate takes her under armed escort, where he reveals to her the Legion's secondary conflicts against the New California Republic, the Great Khans, and the Brotherhood of Steel, before revealing their current conflict over the dirt mound boundary of the camp that is actually a dividing wall, separating them from another opposing camp of legionaries, who are led by another Caesar, a "false" leader in the Lacerta Legate's eyes. The legate elaborates that, ever since the death of the Legion's founder, there has been a war raging to decide who becomes his successor; supposedly, the late Caesar wrote down the name of his heir and kept it close before his passing. Now, his decayed bones lay upon the divide, with both Legion factions violently preventing the other from obtaining the paper, leaving them at a stalemate. The legate declines Lucy's offer to apply her skills at diplomacy to solve their problem, sending her to be crucified and telling Lucy that they find strength to be of greater historical importance than being "good."

entities.name: California Crest Studios
entities.description:
California Crest Studios was a pre-War motion picture company located in the Hollywood district of Los Angeles, California. Its main studio lot appears as a location .

California Crest Studios was founded before the Great War and operated primarily in the Hollywood district of Los Angeles. Its main studio is located not far from a section of the Hollywood Walk of Fame. The company was well known as the makers of the highly successful Western movie The Man from Deadhorse starring Cooper Howard, and had already begun working on a sequel to the film around January 2077. As of that month, they had also signed a deal with the Nuka-Cola Corporation for a seventeen-film series featuring the Nuka-Cola mascots Bottle and Cappy. The studio worked with film services businesses such as catering company Catering to the Stars! and transportation and equipmental rental firm Studio Services, and also operated a bus tour service, California Crest Studio Tours, for tourists visiting its physical location. The company was also known to utilize Mister Handy robotic units in their operations.

Like much of the greater Los Angeles area, the bombs dropping reduced the studio building to rubble, with the desert winds and rolling sands of the wasteland gradually swallowing it up over the years.

In the first of two flashbacks to Cooper's life in the pre-War era, he is filming the final scene of his movie The Man from Deadhorse at the studio but cuts near the end and expresses his discomfort to the film's director Emil Dale about how his sheriff character is scripted to shoot and kill the outlaw played by his co-star Jorge rather than arresting him alive as always happens in his Western films. When Emil fails to convince him of the creative choices behind the decision, Cooper wants to involve one of the writers Cadillac Bob but is informed about the man's firing due to supposedly holding communist beliefs. Cooper's conversation with Emil is cut short when he sees his wife Barb nearby. The loving partners share a touching moment when she tricks him into eating lavender taffy which he hates, before Barb hands him a package containing a Vault jumpsuit to wear for his promotional shoot in collaboration with Barb's employer, the Vault-Tec Corporation. Cooper reluctantly agrees, then opts to race their daughter Janey to his trailer.

Camp Golf is a location in the Mojave Wasteland . In 2281, it is the regional headquarters for the NCR Rangers. It also appears in season 2 of .

Prior to the Great War, the main building was known as the House Resort, with an accompanying golf course belonging to Mr. House. Circa 2277 following the nuclear apocalypse, when the New California Republic began their Mojave Campaign and later came into conflict with Caesar's Legion from the east, the renamed "Camp Golf" was on the frontlines of the First Battle of Hoover Dam.

After the Legion's defeat, however, the camp's strategic value waned as General Oliver drew the bulk of the NCR forces to the Hoover Dam, leaving the resort as the regional headquarters for the NCR Rangers under Chief Hanlon, doubling as a communication and quartermaster hub. This has caused no small amount of tension between the Rangers and troopers as the latter are forced to camp in military tents on the dilapidated golf course, while the former enjoy all the luxuries a pre-War resort provides.

Additionally, owing to the camp's position far from the frontlines of the impending Second Battle of Hoover Dam, it is considered a dumping ground for washouts and poor performers that no commander wants assigned to their garrison. Nevertheless, the NCR maintains a heavy presence, guarding a large water pipe that extends to the north, providing water to the NCR sharecropper farms and ensuring a constant supply of food for the NCR.

Costumes & Fancy Dress is a pre-War business in the American Southwest.

Costumes & Fancy Dress was a costume store located across the street from a football stadium somewhere in the American Southwest. The store contains a poster of the motion picture Revenge of Brutus, as well as mannequins wearing items such as a space suit, Roman gladiator helmets, a cowboy outfit, and a fish costume. The store also seems to have been having a Halloween sale before the bombs dropped.

Dinky the T-Rex is an unmarked location within Novac in the Mojave Wasteland . It also appears in season 2 of , as well as Fallout Shelter.

Dinky has served as a roadside attraction in the area around Novac since before the Great War, additionally serving as a revenue source with the Dino Bite gift shop situated inside of it.

By 2281, the tourist attraction now doubly serves as a sniper's nest, specifically the balcony housed in its jaws, utilized by Novac's resident pair of retired First Recon sharpshooters, Manny Vargas and Craig Boone; both take shifts defending the town during the day and night, respectively.

Situated within the Dino Dee-lite Motel complex, Dinky is situated along Highway 95, visible from a distance due to its height. The T-Rex holds the thermometer, having taken a bite out of the top, that advertises the motel and amenities such as color television.
