entities.name: Dino Dee-lite Motel
entities.description:
The Dino Dee-lite Motel is an unmarked location within Novac in the Mojave Wasteland . It also appears in season 2 of , as well as Fallout Shelter.

A fixture along the route of Highway 95 since before the Great War, the Dino Dee-Lite catered to tourists and travelers, with Dinky the T-Rex serving as a roadside attraction. After the nuclear apocalypse, the motel survived intact but sat vacant for years until the town of Novac was founded around it, taking its name from the broken motel sign by the entrance. By 2281, Jeannie May Crawford serves as the motel's proprietor and takes pride in Novac's small-town appeal.

Situated in the center of Novac, the Dino Dee-lite complex has both a motel and gift shop. The main building is the front desk, which contains the Mojave Express dropbox and serves as the office from which motel rooms are rented. Outside of the entrance to the front desk is the sign displaying the town's name.

Next to the main building's entrance is a gate into a fenced-in area containing the motel rooms and bungalows. Several individuals live in the motel rooms, including Daisy Whitman, Bruce Isaac, Manny Vargas, and Craig Boone. Two of the motel rooms are vacant, and entrance to the room as well as items found within are marked to owned. The second floor of the motel, from left to right while facing the building, contains the player home, a vacant room with a twin bed, Bruce Isaac's room, and Daisy Whitman's room. The first floor, in the same fashion, has Manny Vargas' room, a vacant room with a queen-sized bed, and Boone's room. All other rooms are boarded up and inaccessible.

entities.name: Enclave research colony
entities.description:
The Enclave research colony is a location .

Built before the Great War, the facility has managed to remain under the control of the Enclave by 2296 in spite of multiple failures and defeats suffered by the organization since the mid-23rd century. Enclave experiments seen in the facility include behavioral engineering (using selectively bred dogs in which sub-standard newborns are immediately incinerated), biological research (with captives held in a train car designed for handling live cargo), and energy production via nuclear fusion.

The facility seems to be crucial to some form of overarching Enclave experiment intended to be tested on the surface, with the Vaults themselves supposedly secondary to whatever this experiment is. The facility had a communications network which connected it to several Vault-Tec assets and facilities on the West Coast, including the Vault-Tec headquarters in Los Angeles, California; a management Vault built under Las Vegas, Nevada; and Vault 33 in Santa Monica, California via a Pip-Boy kept by Enclave asset Hank MacLean. Its communications infrastructure also seemingly allowed it to listen on many other radio frequencies used throughout the wasteland.

In 2296, the facility received word from Steph Harper, the wife of Hank MacLean, to begin Phase Two of this experiment.

entities.name: Filly
entities.description:
Filly is a post-War settlement near Los Angeles and a location . It also appears in Fallout Shelter.

Constructed as a town of scrap metal huts in a location close to Santa Monica some time prior to 2296, the Filly town centerpiece is a "giant pile of trash that is slowly sinking into the earth." This ancient landfill, for which the settlement is named, has been steadily mined by Filly's inhabitants since it was founded, allowing them to extract old parts of pre-War technology and scrap to use or sell. By the late 2290s, Filly had gained a reputation both as a focal point for wasteland travel in Los Angeles but also as a place of unchecked violence, as it is known that several people have been killed in the settlement over the years, and beatings and robberies happen in broad daylight with no consequence. The town also prohibits the presence of ghouls.

Sometime prior to or during the destruction of Shady Sands in 2283 by a nuclear detonation, Birdie and her mother had traveled to Filly before moving on as refugees, with an older Birdie claiming that at the time, she could still feel the heat from the explosion that wiped out the NCR capital.

At some point prior to the assault on Vault 33 by the Vault 32 raiders she orchestrated in 2296, Lee Moldaver negotiated with Filly local Ma June to have her act as an intermediary for Siggi Wilzig, a defected Enclave scientist in possession of a cold fusion artifact that Moldaver coveted, for passage through the town to her stronghold at the Griffith Observatory, for which she offered to pay June a thousand caps.

entities.name: Freeside
entities.description:
Freeside is a district of New Vegas in the Mojave Wasteland . It also appears in season 2 of and .

Located within the pre-War ruins of Fremont Street, Freeside has been abandoned by Mr. House and the Three Families as slums condemned to anarchy, with a figurative and literal wall to divide its residents from those House deems worthy of visiting the Strip. Even still, some groups such as the Followers of the Apocalypse and the Van Graffs have made a living for themselves amidst the daily struggle for survival most others face.

While the city of Las Vegas was not heavily damaged during the course of the Great War, survivors did not immediately settle into the remnants of the old city, leaving the ruins to be picked over and fought over by various tribes and raider groups that had descended from Vault dwellers. The Great Khans were forced out of Vegas by the Three Families with the resources of Mr. House, they eventually settled in Bitter Springs. While the Three Families rebuilt the casinos of Vegas, Mr. House employed the rest of the locals to use his sizable quantities of pre-War construction materials to build the crude but effective outer walls that separate the Strip and Freeside from the rest of the surrounding ruins.

While House valued the area around the intersection of Fremont Street and Las Vegas Boulevard, he ultimately viewed it as secondary in importance to the Strip itself and had a second, inner wall built that further separated the two areas. When NCR prospectors arrived in the region, followed soon after by the New California Republic Army, many people typically were heading straight for the Strip and its casinos, leaving "Freeside" (as it had become known by locals) as an informal stopping point. Eventually, Mr. House recognized that he could use Freeside as a filter for undesirables and pulled all his resources out of the area, save for a token Securitron force to guard the sole entryway into the Strip while leaving Freeside to fend for itself.

entities.name: Griffith Observatory
entities.description:
Griffith Observatory is a post-War settlement and location .

Prior to the Great War, Griffith Observatory was sponsored by the Vault-Tec Corporation and designated as a "Science & Friendship Center." The observatory was able to survive the devastation caused by the nuclear strikes on Los Angeles, although it suffered some structural damage along with wear and tear over the following 200 years.

Around 2283, a nuclear bomb destroyed the New California Republic capital of Shady Sands. The NCR presence in Los Angeles subsequently declined; however, surviving NCR forces who were not in Shady Sands when it was destroyed coalesced under the leadership of Lee Moldaver, a pre-War scientist and notable figure in Shady Sands prior to its destruction. She led them to garrison the old observatory, which became the last known remaining NCR headquarters in Los Angeles, housing both civilians and NCR soldiers.

There, she hoped to restore the ruined Shady Sands' prospects by building a cold fusion reactor using technology she herself had created over 200 years ago. However, the reactor required two essential components: the first was a cold fusion diode, and the second were the credentials of a pre-War Vault-Tec employee. The credentials were needed to activate the reactor inside the observatory, as the cold fusion technology had become proprietary to Vault-Tec before the Great War.

entities.name: Hawthorne Medical Laboratories
entities.description:
Hawthorne Medical Laboratories is a location .

Founded in the pre-War era, Hawthorne Medical Laboratories was a subsidiary of the Vault-Tec Corporation. Its main campus in Los Angeles, California was connected to the structure of Vault 4, which was designed as a research facility to be overseen by HML leaders Lloyd and Cassandra Hawthorne. The exterior entrance of Vault 4 was built not far from the Hawthorne Medical Laboratories campus, with the two locations in visible distance of each other.

To aid in the radiation and genetics experiments of the Vault's head researchers, the surface-level building was altered such that a hallway just inside from the main entrance was turned into a booby-trapped chamber, luring people in by using a fake door labeled as the entrance to a medical storage wing, then dropping them down a chute into a decontamination room within Vault 4 where they would be processed as new test subjects.

Due to Maximus' health declining from a wound he sustained during the ambush by fiends Javin and Rink, Lucy helps him search for medical supplies. They eventually reach the grounds of Hawthorne Medical Laboratories, though do not notice the signage marking it as a Vault-Tec property. After Lucy fails to re-emerge from scouting ahead, Maximus enters himself and is caught in the booby trap that brings him and Lucy into Vault 4.

entities.name: Headquarters of the United Nations
entities.description:
The headquarters of the United Nations is a mentioned-only location and .

In May 2052, as Earth's fossil fuel supplies began to dry up and nations began to wage war with each other over the few resources that remained, the United Nations began to collapse under intense international squabbling, with many heated debates breaking out within their headquarters in New York City.

On July 26, 2052, at the height of global tensions over resource availability, the organization was formally disbanded. The sitting UN President at the time, Sakugama Okiri, lamented the failure of global relations at a press conference held later in the building. The ambassadors of the few nations that remained in the headquarters were forced to vacate by the end of the week as a bidding war broke out over the building itself. As reported in the D.C.-based Capital Post newspaper, the toy company Bumbalo's, in particular, hoped to turn the prime real estate into their new East Coast superstore.

Although the eventual buyer is unknown, training guides produced by the Vault-Tec Corporation included a cartoon depiction of the UN building being overtaken with Vault-Tec logos. It remains unclear if this is a reflection of reality or merely a hyperbolic appropriation of the UN's imagery.

entities.name: Hollywood
entities.description:
Hollywood was a municipality of Los Angeles that was known for its celebrities and film productions before the Great War.

Before the War, Hollywood was known for being the site of numerous film studios and productions, to the point that the word "Hollywood" itself was synonymous with the American film industry. Countless actors and directors found success in Hollywood, creating movies of all genres, ranging from Westerns and noir dramas to romances, sci-fi, and horror flicks. Hollywood was also known for its celebrity culture, being a gathering place for film stars and other high-profile personalities. It was frequently associated with scandalous or borderline scandalous activities, with substance abuse and "compromising" romantic situations (such as one witnessed by Keith McKinney between director Sergio Amore and actor Vince Natali in a nightclub) being little more than the "usual Hollywood tune."

By the 2070s, however, with wartime tensions and corporate power at an all-time high, some of the luster started to fade. Many figures in the film industry were either affiliated to communism or otherwise disagreed with the propaganda; whatever the case, they were all lumped together as radicals who opposed the United States. These supposed ties could cost people their reputations (such as with actors Charles Whiteknife and Cooper Howard), if not their jobs (as with screenwriter Cadillac Bob), regardless of their accuracy. Some studios recognized the winds of public opinion and even rewrote entire films just to present themselves as patriotic, as with California Crest Studios and their box office-topping Western The Man from Deadhorse.

Meanwhile, corporations began turning to Hollywood celebrities to further their business through promotional deals, celebrity endorsements, and/or product enhancement. Cooper Howard became the public face of the Vault-Tec Corporation for some time (by October 23, 2077, he had been labeled as a communist and replaced with Vault Boy), while English actor Sebastian Leslie sold his vocal rights to RobCo for their Mister Handies, and the Nuka-Cola Corporation entered a deal with California Crest Studios to produce an entire seventeen-picture series of films featuring their mascots, Bottle and Cappy. As Sebastian Leslie saw it, the future was entirely in products, and anyone who refused to acknowledge this would only be left in the dust.

entities.name: Hollywood Boulevard
entities.description:
In the era before the Great War, Hollywood Boulevard was famous as a cultural icon of the Hollywood district of Los Angeles, California, running through many tourist areas. Museums, landmarks, and more defined its attraction.

After the bombs struck, a large part of the boulevard located off of Exit 12A from a nearby highway became submerged and surrounded by overgrown forests, with the concrete skeletons of old, stripped buildings still popping out of the water; by 2296, several have collapsed and sunk below the surface. A population of deer is present in the area, preyed upon by other creatures inhabiting the flooded areas, such as leeches.

By 2296, the flooded area had become home to at least one gulper, mutant creatures originally created by radiation experiments in Vault 4's Level 12 laboratory, some of which evidently managed to escape from the Vault at some point after the Great War.

While carrying the decapitated head of Siggi Wilzig on her solo trek to find Moldaver, Lucy MacLean reaches the flooded shores of the Boulevard where she is briefly amazed by the peripheral view of the area, then spots a baby deer drinking by the lakeside. She tries to feed it some grass and admire the peaceful atmosphere until a gulper strikes fast from the lake, dragging the deer into the water from behind a thicket of tall grass and forcing Lucy to equip her tranq gun.

entities.name: Hollywood Forever
entities.description:
Hollywood Forever was constructed in the namesake Hollywood district of Los Angeles, California, consisting of a cemetery, funeral home, and crematorium. The business offered consultations for potential customers. In the late 21st century, the central mausoleum was used as a secret meeting place for an anti-capitalist group organized by "Miss Williams" that included prominent Hollywood figures such as actor Charles Whiteknife.

For unknown reasons, a tunnel was built into the undercroft of the mausoleum, with its other end located somewhere in or near Griffith Observatory.

What is shown of the location post-War indicates that, though the standing structures and most of the headstones collapsed from damage by the bombs or wear and tear over time, the landscape itself was left largely intact, including the secret tunnel to the observatory.

Around the mid-to-late 2070s, Cooper Howard, with some prompting from his friend Charles Whiteknife, drives to Hollywood Forever to attend the meeting of an anti-capitalist, supposedly communist group that Charles told him would provide some clarity on Cooper's doubts over his ties to the Vault-Tec Corporation. He meets his friend in the hall where Cooper also has a personal encounter with the group's leader, a woman known only as "Miss Williams" who claims to be "a big fan" of his films.

The Hollywood Sign was originally erected in 1923 on Mount Lee near the Hollywood district in Los Angeles California, where it initially spelled out "Hollywoodland" until later being shortened to "Hollywood." Since then, it became recognized as an iconic symbol of the district's global fame as an American entertainment hub. At some point in the 21st century, the Nuka-Cola Corporation secured sponsorship of the sign in return for the construction of a giant neon sign reading "Sponsored by Nuka-Cola" erected just below the sign itself.

The Hollywood Sign and its corporate-sponsored subtitle lasted intact through the Great War and 219 years of exposure to the elements and wear and tear, with the electrical systems for its lighting rig remaining intact as well.

In 2296, shortly after Lee Moldaver activates her cold fusion reactor at Griffith Observatory to restore power to the ruins of Los Angeles, the resulting surge of electrical power reaches the Hollywood sign just after Lucy MacLean, the Ghoul, and CX404 exit an escape tunnel into Hollywood Forever, showing off the sign as still being intact as well as the name of its long-defunct corporate sponsorship.

Before the Great War, the House Resort and Country Club was one of the properties in the Las Vegas area owned by and named for Robert House.

Managing to survive the nuclear apocalypse in remarkable condition, circa. 2277 when the New California Republic began their Mojave Campaign and moved into the region, the resort and its associated golf course were occupied and renamed "Camp Golf." During the First Battle of Hoover Dam against Caesar's Legion coming east across the Colorado River, Camp Golf was on the frontlines and saw heavy action but ultimately continued to survive after the Legion's defeat.

By 2281, due to the bulk of the NCR forces being moved to garrison the Hoover Dam for the impending Second Battle of Hoover Dam, the resort has been left in the hands of the New California Republic Rangers led by Chief Hanlon as their regional HQ, serving as both a communications and quartermaster hub. However, the Rangers' occupying the resort has caused no small amount of tension between them and the NCR troopers that live in military tents out on the dilapidated golf course.

entities.description:
The King's School of Impersonation is an unmarked location within Freeside in the Mojave Wasteland.

Prior to the Great War, the building was host to an Elvis Presley impersonation school that served the greater Las Vegas area. It included the use of holotapes and outfits to teach how to mimic his voice and fashion as well as a classroom curriculum that taught how to replicate his speech patterns and catchphrases, and even what kind of foods he liked to eat.

Following the nuclear apocalypse, the building, like most of the area around Vegas was left to rot and ruin until 2274, when Mr. House emerged from the Lucky 38 with his Securitrons to establish New Vegas ahead of the arrival of the New California Republic. He issued an ultimatum to the tribals and raiders living in the ruins, ultimately recruiting those who became the Three Families while the rest were either evicted or killed.

One of the tribal groups tried to eke out a living in the slums but found firsthand how rough living could be. They eventually came across the King's School of Impersonation and learned about the image and ideals of one called "the King" (they never learned his real name as all evidence had been unintelligbly degraded). Inspired, the tribals reinvented themselves as the Kings, led by The King, based around the anarchic ideal of complete personal freedom, where "every man is a king in [their] own right."

entities.description:
The radio station was constructed at the base of Hollywood Hills near the city of Los Angeles, on a forested hill surrounded by desert.

By the late 2290s, the sole occupant of KPSS is the radio host Carl, who fills the airtime entirely with a large collection of vintage fiddle music. Carl does not take visitors at the station, with an array of defensive traps, including massive bear traps and makeshift crossbows linked to tripwires, surrounding the main building to ensure anyone looking to place a request or make a complaint about his choice of music would sooner have an arrow lodged in their vital parts. The station exterior is littered with the displayed heads of those Carl refers to as his "critics."

After abandoning CX404 at the Red Rocket gas station, Thaddeus eventually arrives at the radio station carrying Siggi Wilzig's head and requests the usage of Carl's broadcasting equipment to get a message to the Brotherhood of Steel for retrieval, meanwhile complimenting his choice of music and booby trap setup.

Sometime later, he spots Lucy MacLean and Maximus approaching and, still viewing the latter as a traitor to the Brotherhood, attempts to shoot at them with his 10mm pistol but misses every shot. While stumbling back, Thaddeus ends up triggering one of Carl's traps and gets a crossbow bolt shot through his neck. He only survives the wound due to the snake oil salesman's elixir that he consumed.

entities.name: Las Vegas management Vault
entities.description:
The Las Vegas management Vault is a location in season 2 of the Fallout TV series.

This facility was one of a series of special vaults for management employees of the Vault-Tec Corporation to oversee the other mainline Vaults. It was one of many such facilities, along with one built somewhere in Oregon and another somewhere in California. While officially a Vault-Tec facility, it was secretly constructed for their financiers, the Enclave.

The facility was built half a mile underneath Las Vegas, Nevada, accessible from the Lucky 38 via a series of subterranean tunnels. Robert House, who was aware that nuclear war was inevitable and took steps to preserve Las Vegas from the bombs, permitted Vault-Tec to build this vault, but then "rigged" it in some way to make sure the company could not use it for their plans. It is not specified what House did, but he is shown to have control over at least some of the management Vault's systems through his mainframe.

At the Las Vegas management vault, research was undertaken on the Black Box chip technology developed by House, which he had licensed to Vault-Tec in exchange for ownership of their cold fusion diode. The management Vault's researchers specifically worked on miniaturizing the chip's hardware while maintaining its functionality, with experiments on live test subjects including both mice and humans. However, they evidently were not able to overcome the technology's flaw of causing subjects' heads to overload and explode when receiving more complex commands.

Many aircraft crashed around the airport and its surrounding terrain during the Great War. Airplane parts have also been scavenged and/or salvaged for settlements such as Filly. At some point, a satellite owned by the Soviet Union also crashed near the airport. There was a donut shop located along a road not far from the airport.

Owned and operated by the namesake Ma June for some time prior to 2296, the general goods store serves as a mainstay of the trading town of Filly in New California. In addition to various bits and bobs including old Vault-Tec products and merchandise, June also keeps a selection of weapons behind the store counter for sale including plasma pistols, a Junk Jet, laser muskets, etc. Due to the collapse of the New California Republic's economy around the greater Los Angeles area following the destruction of Shady Sands in 2283, stores like Ma June's returned to the tried-and-true barter system utilizing bottle caps with a prohibition on refunds.

Lucy enters Ma June's Sundries and, at first, comments about how Ma June was selling Vault-Tec items and surmises that she must do business with criminals. Aside from Lucy's interest in a particular criminal, Ma June was more interested in the fact that Lucy was a Vault dweller and tried to call on her roommate Barv. As Lucy tries to ask Ma June about the criminal she is looking for, while Ma June beckons Barv, Lucy alerts Ma June when she drops Moldaver's name.

After closing her ledger and telling Barv to return to her room, Ma June then debates Lucy about her Vault naivete, who begs Ma June for any information on Moldaver. In the end, Ma June kicks Lucy out of her store, but as Lucy leaves, she runs into Siggi Wilzig, who she met at her campfire the other night in front of the store.

The two would briefly talk until Ma June walked out of her store. After confirming Wilzig's identity, she told him to enter her store and demanded that Lucy scram. However, the Ghoul, who sat on a chair close by to the store, accosts Wilzig, blows off his left foot, and in retaliation, Ma June puts a bounty on the Ghoul's head.

There are shelves on the wall to the right of where Mick is standing, and a central "shelf" made of washing machines in the middle of the room. To the right of Mick is a staircase that leads to a room upstairs that comprises Mick and Ralph's bedrooms and a few other items such as washing machines and desks. entities.name: Santa Monica
entities.description:
Santa Monica was a pre-War city in Los Angeles County, California.

Before the Great War, Santa Monica was a coastal city and a famous tourist destination, mostly for the Santa Monica Pier, located not far from a downtown promenade and a mall. By January 2077, it had reportedly been described as one of the best places to live by various trade publications. The city was chosen by the Vault-Tec Corporation to house Vault 33, which was constructed just south of the Santa Monica Pier in a bunker-like building along the coast. Vault 31 and Vault 32, which together with Vault 33 formed the Three Vaults, were also built in the vicinity of Santa Monica.

By 2296, the area directly surrounding the Santa Monica Pier had mostly turned to desert. The pier itself is largely still standing, along with the husks of some buildings scattered around its periphery. The ruins of larger buildings that were once part of Santa Monica's urban environment are still present further in-land.

Santa Monica appears in the Fallout television series, although the area corresponding to it is visible on the first Fallout game's world map as well.

The entrance to Vault 33 was built just slightly further inland from the pier.

As of 2296, much of the pier up to its Ferris wheel is still standing, but the sections further past have collapsed into the ocean. entities.name: Silver Rush
entities.description:
The Silver Rush is an unmarked location within Freeside in the Mojave Wasteland . It also appears in season 2 of .

Established in 2071, the Silver Rush Casino rivaled the Atomic Wrangler Casino on their shared space along Fremont Street in Las Vegas, Nevada.

Following the Great War, new owners reestablished the old casino sometime prior to 2281, even reigniting the old rivalry with the Atomic Wrangler. That lasted until the arrival of the Van Graffs in the Mojave seeking to expand their arms-trading business. Setting their sights on the Silver Rush, the Van Graffs swept in and "evicted" the former owners, throwing out all the casino hardware to make room for their stockpile of energy weapons. When the Kings showed up to protest the change in management, the Van Graffs gave them a first-hand taste of their weaponry, reducing some of their number to goo, after which the two groups have left each other alone ever since.

Initially, the Silver Rush weapons depot was headed by Frieda Van Graff, but she soon left to pursue personal interests. After Frieda's departure, her sister Gloria Van Graff and brother Jean-Baptiste Cutting were assigned to head the Silver Rush. They soon capitalized on the Silver Rush's proximity to the Atomic Wrangler by forgoing any sort of rivalry and instead making it attractive to the casino's customers with pockets full of caps from gambling.

entities.name: Sonny's Sundries
entities.description:
A general store within Freeside, Sonny's Sundries sold various items including sundries, weapons, medicine, and other equipment. It was owned and operated by Sonny up until July 2296, when Sonny was murdered by a thief named Simon. Simon subsequently took over, pretending to be the shopkeeper by putting on Sonny's clothes, which were far too small for him, and heavily inflating Sonny's prices. Sonny's remains were shoved into a garbage bin inside near the back of the store.

Suffering from a Buffout addiction, Lucy MacLean is given bottle caps by the Ghoul, who tells her to go to Sonny's Sundries to purchase Addictol with which to clean out her system. When she reaches the store, she sees that the price for Addictol, written on a chalkboard outside the main door, has been raised to a degree that she cannot afford.

Lucy is disheartened, but sees a back door left open on the side of the shop, and decides that to deal with her present circumstances she must steal a vial of Addictol from the store. Sneaking in, she finds the medicine, takes it, and pauses to inspect and additionally take a power fist on display, as well as a bag to hold it. While she does so, she notices a dead and bloody body stuffed into a nearby trash can—that of Sonny, though Lucy is initially unaware of this.

While distracted, Shopkeep Simon sees her and confronts her, and Lucy tries to assuage the man and come across as a regular shopper. As she does so, she notices a portrait of the store owner, the dead man in the trash can. She inquires about the dead body, which Simon unconvincingly claims was an attempted thief. Lucy questions him why the man is naked, which causes Simon to defensively claim that naked robbers aren't unusual. She questions him further about why his clothes don't fit and deduces the body in the trash can is the original shopkeeper, pulling her 10mm pistol on Simon. She tries to avoid further escalation but doesn't hesitate to shoot Simon as he immediately reaches for a weapon. Lucy inspects him, finding she had shot him dead and starts reconsidering her recent actions, taking the Addictol and power fist and leaving soon after a customer arrives to find her standing over Simon's corpse.

entities.description:
Originally built by the Soviet Union before the Great War, it was launched into orbit around the Earth, though any functions it may have carried out during this time are unknown. The satellite is painted red and was powered by two solar panels. The bottom of the satellite housed what seems to be a sophisticated camera and communications system, indicating that it was built largely for surveillance purposes. The camera was a large red spherical structure with the Russian abbreviation "СССР" emblazoned onto it.

Sometime after the bombs fell in 2077, the satellite underwent orbital reentry and suffered significant damage when it landed in the flat plains close to the ruins of Los Angeles International Airport in New California but remained mostly intact, with some parts of its machinery still clearly visible.

After escaping from the Ghoul in Filly, Lucy MacLean attempts to escort Siggi Wilzig across the plains near the old airport, however, he was slowed due to an injured leg shoddily "repaired" with a Jim's Limbs prosthetic that was causing him to deteriorate from blood loss. At some point before they reached the site of the crashed satellite, Wilzig ingested a Plan D cyanide pill to hasten his demise. Once this fact was revealed, he implores Lucy to use his surgical Ripper and remove his head containing the cold fusion artifact in order to carry it the rest of the way to Moldaver before passing away. After initial reluctance, Lucy performs the surgical removal and leaves the headless body propped up against the old satellite, where it is later found by the Ghoul who was following after CX404 and her canine nose detecting Wilzig's scent.

Wilzig's corpse and the satellite are visited for a third time by Thaddeus and Maximus (disguised as Knight Titus) who discern that the artifact they were sent to find for the Brotherhood of Steel is embedded in the deceased's head, sending them after Lucy and the Ghoul.

The factory was constructed by the Sunset Sarsaparilla Company on a hilltop elevated above and overlooking the city of Las Vegas, Nevada and was neighbored by a motel business. What is shown of the present-day area indicates it survived the Great War intact with little, if any radiation affecting it.

At some point, a RobCo Securitron ended up at the factory for unknown reasons. By 2296, a combination of age and lack of maintenance resulted in its programming going haywire, causing it to erratically shift between thinking it was a masseuse and a security guard.

Sometime after escaping from the KPSS radio station near Hollywood Hills, the mutated ex-Brotherhood squire Thaddeus left New California and made his way to the Mojave Wasteland where he discovered the abandoned factory. His exploration included finding its malfunctioning "security guard" which he chose to stay apart from but still keep around for protection. With his access to the bottling floor, Thaddeus decided to set up a cap collecting operation; to maximize profit, he installed himself as floor manager and gathered a "crew" of orphaned human and ghoul children to man the conveyor belts bringing out crates of soda so they could pry off the caps while drinking the leftover soda for refreshment.

The bombs dropping in 2077 spared much of the building itself, though it was seemingly looted of much of its inventory by scavengers over the years.

Sometime prior to 2296, the abandoned building was taken over by wastelanders Huey and Squirrel and set up as a "legitimate" business selling medical supplies including inhaler vials. To accrue a supply of the vials, they also entered into the market of organ-harvesting by hiring bounty hunters to capture ghoul and human wastelanders alike, relying on a repurposed Mister Handy unit, Snip Snip, to perform the crude surgical operations.

At some point, Sorrel Booker's Govermint secured Huey and Squirrel's operation under a protection racket, involving the occasional visit by Govermint "sheriffs" to collect their cut of the profits while handling any troublemakers that could disrupt business.

The Ghoul escorts a captive Lucy MacLean across the wasteland from Hollywood Boulevard to the Super Duper Mart in order to sell her to the organ-harvesters in exchange for a resupply of inhaler vials after losing them to the gulper. Shortly after Lucy enters the fortified building, he collapses outside from withdrawal.

entities.name: The Ghoul's grave
entities.description:
At some point, the Ghoul was captured by a powerful man known as Dom Pedro and brought to his stronghold. Considering the Ghoul a personal enemy, Dom Pedro had him buried alive in a grave, sustained only by an IV drip. Dom Pedro would dig up the Ghoul annually, cut off pieces of his body, and rebury him.

Sometime in 2296, a group of bounty hunters consisting of Honcho, Biggie, and Slim snuck into Dom Pedro's fortress at night. Biggie used his Junk Jet to take out a guard. Honcho explains that they are searching for a notorious bounty hunter whom Dom Pedro has held captive for several years.

They come upon a small graveyard containing one grave with a pair of IV bags and tubes emerging from the dirt. Biggie and Slim are shocked to realize the person they are looking for is a ghoul. Honcho reassures them, mentioning that his father once worked with the Ghoul. Biggie expresses concern that he may have gone feral, prompting Honcho to bring out a chicken to test him, as feral ghouls cannot tolerate them.

The hunters dig up the coffin and open it after placing the chicken in front of it. The Ghoul emerges, revealed to be an aged and mutated Cooper Howard. He playfully picks up the chicken, terrifying Biggie and Slim. Honcho proposes they work together to secure a large bounty on the target, who has gone to seek out Moldaver in California. The Ghoul takes offense at the mention of his past and claims that, unlike them, he pursues bounties "for the love of the game." He then kills Slim and Biggie, wounds Honcho, and drags him over to toss him into the coffin before letting it drop back into the open grave. The Ghoul spares the chicken and takes it with him as he leaves to pursue the bounty alone.

entities.name: Ultra-Luxe
entities.description:
The Ultra-Luxe Las Vegas Resort, typically shortened to just the Ultra-Luxe, is an unmarked location within the New Vegas Strip . While the exterior may affect the idea of an oasis of refinement and decadence amidst the dust and grime of the post-nuclear world, with food that puts the average wastelander's sense of taste to shame in the Gourmand restaurant, behind closed doors the governing White Glove Society tries to rise above the dark past of their tribal days, of which they are contractually obligated to keep locked away behind those doors.

One of the more luxurious establishments on the Strip, built roughly at the same time as the Tops casino, the Ultra-Luxe was touted as featuring the finest quality accommodations and a world-class restaurant, the Gourmand, all to provide its patrons with the highest possible quality of service and living.

In the establishment's pre-War history, a mob shootout took place in the casino on July 13, 2072. Eyewitnesses provided conflicting details, but sources agreed that it was a chaotic situation, that all five of the mobsters were killed and seventeen bystanders were injured. The Las Vegas chief of police claimed the incident as a major victory.

Even after the Great War, the Ultra-Luxe continues as an establishment of ineradicable refinement that delicately conceals its operators' more questionable past tendencies. The staff pampers its clients and provides The Strip's most elite casino experience. Among its members, the dress code is strictly enforced as the White Glove Society are all well-dressed, well-spoken, and well-behaved. The casino's prime attractions are its meat-oriented restaurant, The Gourmand; its cocktail lounge, Top Shelf, and its art gallery. On the casino floor, there are no slot machines and only Roulette and Blackjack are offered for gambling. As Mr. House himself describes it; "[They] put together one hell of a resort hotel, too. From what I hear, I'd want to eat at the Gourmand every night... if I were ambulatory."

The Uranium City Internment Camp is a location .

Before the Great War, this internment camp was operated by the United States Armed Forces to detain Canadian citizens during or after the United States annexation of Canada. Military personnel, including U.S. Marines, were used in controlling the population of the camp.

At some point, a mass escape occurred at the camp, seemingly due to an attack by Canadian partisans.

Steph Harper and her mother escape from the internment camp along with other Canadians. They are chased by guards who fire at them. Steph and her mother are discovered by a Vertibird and a Marine in power armor who tells them to return to the camp or he will shoot, while using the slur "Hoser" to describe them. Before either party can react, a suicide bomber kills the soldier, although Steph's mother is mortally wounded. She tells Steph to get south and survive, while telling her not to worry if she harms anyone to do so, as she shouldn't think of them as human beings, but Americans.

entities.name: Vault 4
entities.description:
Vault 4 is a Vault-Tec Vault located beneath the Hawthorne Medical Laboratories campus in Los Angeles, California .

Before the Great War, Vault 4 was featured in advertisements and Vault orientation videos, with Cooper Howard serving as the spokesman. The Vault's experiment was publicly revealed in these advertisements: it would be governed by scientists living and working there full-time (technocracy). Lloyd and Cassandra Hawthorne, two prominent researchers on the effects of radiation on DNA, as well as their two children and 80 other volunteers, signed up to live in the Vault for a five-year trial before the Great War to show that society would survive even in a Vault. Lloyd Hawthorne eventually became the Vault's overseer after the Great War.

Sealed on the day of the Great War, the Vault became a part of the Vault experiment, examining the performance of a society governed entirely by scientists with no limits on their control and decisions. However, the Vault's governance by scientists led to unrestricted research, including human testing, which led to the scientists' downfall. Luring wastelanders into the Vault, the scientists subjected them to mutation experiments, including hybridizing humans with radiation-resistant species, leading to the creation of creatures such as gulpers.

Each experiment was carefully recorded for analysis, including one of the victims of these experiments giving birth to a school of gulpers, who proceeded to eat her alive in the birth tank. The horrific nature of the experimentation led to a rebellion by the test subjects, who unleashed the mutated victims on the scientists. Overseer Hawthorne and his wife tried to barricade themselves outside the specimen laboratory, but the gulpers managed to break through the barricade, eating them both alive. In his final log, the overseer was unapologetic, insisting that hybridizing humans with radioactive-resistant species still had potential, as did a society governed entirely by scientists.

entities.name: Vault 24
entities.description:
Vault 24 is a Vault-Tec Vault located in the Mojave Wasteland. It appears as a location , while a jumpsuit from the Vault was cut from .

right|220px|thumb|The Ghoul picks up an ushanka with a red star, the international symbol of communism. Vault 24 was designed to preserve and continue research into mind-control technologies, with Vault-Tec's experimental staff using Americans assigned to the Vault as test subjects once the protocol was initiated. While they experimented with a variety of surgical techniques and reconditioning, the most successful was the brain-computer interface chip or "black box": American dwellers fitted with this device were successfully converted to communism, replacing Vault-Tec and American iconography with the flags of China, communist propaganda, and eschewing Vault jumpsuits in favor of simple two-piece red garments with a prominent red star on the left-hand side and an ushanka with another red star bordered in gold.

The Vault eventually failed, although the reasons for the failure are unclear. By 2296, mummified corpses of Vault dwellers litter the halls, some found still gathered at tables during what might be a council or soviet meeting, others still strapped to gurneys and medical chairs in the research laboratories, once forcibly made to watch videos meant to recondition them, with electrodes implanted into their brains.

Once his true nature was revealed by Lee Moldaver, the escaped Hank MacLean made his way to Vault 24 to seize the Vault's treasure trove of research. Vault laboratory 7HSZMS380200313 and the Vault itself was abandoned by this time, and he successfully took the data drive with him. Lucy MacLean and the Ghoul subsequently tracked him to the Vault, finding evidence of the Vault experiment within, and an unfortunate victim of Hank's, who was used as a test subject to verify the functionality of the black box and leave a message for his daughter in gruesome fashion.

entities.name: Vault 32
entities.description:
Vault 32 is a location and Vault-Tec Vault in Los Angeles, California .

One of the interconnected Three Vaults near Santa Monica, Los Angeles, Vault 32 was directly connected with Vault 31 and 33. However, direct contact between the populations was limited - officially to prevent the spread of threats, but with the ability to come to each other's aid in times of need. The Vault remained sealed after the Great War, only exchanging population and necessary supplies with its sister Vaults. For decades, the dwellers were told that the surface was uninhabitable, but encouraged to prepare themselves for the eventual Reclamation Day.

The situation was stable for over two centuries, as entire generations were born, lived, and died underground. However, a crisis struck in 2294, as the dwellers of Vault 32 learned that they were actually guinea pigs, rats in a maze, existing solely for the purpose of Bud Askins' eugenics project at Vault 31. where selected graduates of his Bud's Buds executive training program would be placed in a state of cryostasis in Vault 31, and then cross-bred with selected candidates from Vaults 32 and 33, all under Bud's supervision, as the robot overseer of 31. In essence, 32 and 33 were just breeding pools.

To keep the populations docile, all overseers of 32 and 33 were thawed junior executives from Vault 31, awakened periodically and transferred to the other two Vaults, before replacing their predecessors through supposedly democratic elections or appointments. The consistent selection of overseers from Vault 31 was not a secret. Still, none of the dwellers truly questioned it, ascribing it to the superior education and resources of Vault 31, as well as the slogan "When things look glum, vote 31." It's not clear how the dwellers learned of the secret, but Overseer Ian Jackson was tortured to death and his staff hanged. At the same time, the resulting violence across the Vault led to widespread loss of life as they split into factions and started killing each other or committing suicide. Graffiti painted on the walls was a stark reminder to others that the dwellers knew the truth and what was inside 31, promising death to Management (Askins' eugenics project). The anti-Management faction appears to have prevailed and attempted to force their way into Vault 31, using whatever tools they had at hand, including blowtorches and other construction equipment. However, the revolt ultimately failed, with the dwellers perishing at the Vault door.

entities.name: Vault 33
entities.description:
Vault 33 is a Vault in what was once Santa Monica . Its entrance is located shortly south of the Santa Monica Pier. Along with Vault 31 and Vault 32, it is one of the "Three Vaults" linked by a triangle of tunnels.

Betty Pearson is the Vault's overseer as of July 2296, replacing Hank MacLean. Hank's daughter Lucy and son Norm MacLean are two of the main protagonists of the Fallout TV series.

Vault 33 is an experimental Vault built in Santa Monica, California. It is implied Vault 33 may have been built into a subway as it is called a subway vault. It was built to have a maximum capacity of 220 residents. The Vault was unveiled in January 2077 in a special televised broadcast by the Galaxy News Network, though the broadcast was plagued by technical difficulties which forced its host to fill time for an hour until the Vault was finally able to be opened for the grand showcase.

Vault 33 is unique in that it forms a part of a network of three Vaults; it is connected directly to its sister Vaults: Vault 31 and Vault 32. To prevent the spread of threats (e.g., infectious disease), the three Vaults are isolated from one another, except for periodic trade (happening every three years, known as the Triennial Trade) and situations where the Vaults come to each other's aid. The Vault functions as a democracy like its sister Vaults, with the overseer chosen by the community in popular elections for four-year terms, advised by a three-member Vault council. Its dwellers are told that the surface is unfit for recolonization due to radiation levels and instead encouraged to bond with each other and the other two Vaults.

entities.name: Vault-Tec headquarters
entities.description:
The Vault-Tec headquarters, also called the Vault-Tec building, is a location .

Located in Los Angeles in southern California, the building was one of the Vault-Tec Corporation's headquarters and housed the offices of executives such as Barb Howard and Bud Askins, who oversaw the company's Southern California operations.

After the Great War, the building was left abandoned, with the corpses of pre-War employees still strewn about. In 2296, following the destruction of Filly by the Knights of San Fernando, former Filly residents Ma June and Barv moved into the lobby of the Vault-Tec headquarters, claiming it as their new squat and radroach farm.

The Vault-Tec building is a large skyscraper designed in a Mid-Century Modern architectural style, located somewhere within Los Angeles. There is a parking lot in front of the main entrance, leading into a lobby with elevators adjacent to the reception desk. A conference room was at the back of the ground floor. Elsewhere in the building, there were a set of adjoining communications rooms. Barb Howard's office was in another space nearby. There was also a room, presumably adjacent to Barb's office, that was used as a waiting room by Cooper Howard when he visited to spy on his wife.

During the trek from Hollywood Boulevard to a Super Duper Mart near Santa Monica Boulevard, the Ghoul and Lucy MacLean pass near the Westside Medical Clinic and overhear someone shouting inside. entities.description:
The region known as the "Wilds" is shown to be a vast stretch of New California which includes some pre-War cityscapes of Los Angeles that have been retaken by nature, distinguished by its dense woods punctuated by overgrown urban structures, home to populations of wildlife including hostile mutated types such as gulpers and yao guai.

In 2296, after escaping initial capture during his defection from the Enclave and subsequent flight from their mountainous research colony, Siggi Wilzig and his canine companion CX404 pass through the Wilds on a trek to reach the trading town of Filly. They eventually come to a clearing outside a cave where Wilzig tries to consume a trail ration of Cram but is interrupted by his dog returning with a severed human hand and subsequently run off by nearby danger.

Wilzig's escape was later discovered by the Commonwealth Brotherhood of Steel, who gave orders to a Brotherhood chapter called the Knights of San Fernando, assigning them the mission of capturing Wilzig and his artifact. On the order of the San Fernando chapter's leader, Elder Cleric Quintus, several teams of knights and their squires were sent to scour the Wilds in search of the Enclave defector.

One such team, composed of Knight Titus and his squire Maximus (replacing the original pick Dane) disembarks from their vertibird in the section of the Wilds that Wilzig passed through. After coming across the scientist's campsite, the two investigate the cave suspecting that their target had been attacked and killed by its inhabitant. Subsequently, Titus is ambushed by the nesting yao guai, disarmed of his heavy assault rifle, and attempts to flee in terror but is chased down and lethally mauled by the creature.

Sometime prior to 2296, a yao guai claimed the cave as its nest. It preyed on surrounding wildlife and even several wastelanders with their bones and gory remains left strewn around inside.

Sometime after escaping from the Enclave research colony, Siggi Wilzig and his companion CX404 passed through the Wilds and came to a rest outside the cave. While Wilzig had a trail ration of Cram, the canine wandered into the cave where it retrieved a severed human hand to bring back to its master. entities.description:
Babylon was the capital city of Babylonia, a kingdom in ancient Mesopotamia.

When speaking with Joshua Graham, he recites a passage from the Bible that mentions Babylon. Gameplay-wise, there is an achievement called O Daughter of Babylon.

The gardener and mammologist exams at the Pioneer Scout camp have questions that also reference the kingdom. A question in the gardener exam asks, "Mary wants to grow a spectacular garden, with all the best plants she can find. She wants to model her garden off of a legendary Wonder of the World. Which garden should she use as her model?" The Hanging Gardens of Babylon is provided as the correct answer to the question. Additionally, a question in the mammologist exam asks, "Snippers is a good house cat. He eats his food and uses his litter box, just like he's supposed to. Which ancient country can we thank for domesticating cats like Snippers?" Babylon is provided as an incorrect answer to the question.

Babylon is mentioned in the Fallout: New Vegas add-on Honest Hearts and in the Fallout 76 update Wild Appalachia.

When speaking with Blind Diode Jefferson, he claims he can program the Sonic emitter with waves that would make "Jericho look like a kazoo."

Jericho is mentioned only in the Fallout: New Vegas add-on Old World Blues.

Blind Diode Jefferson's line is a reference to the biblical tale of the Battle of Jericho, in which the Canaanite stronghold was captured after the Israelites surrounded the city and blew their horns, causing the walls to fall.

entities.name: Rub' al Khali
entities.description:
The Rub' al Khali, which translates into English as the Empty Quarter, is the largest contiguous sand desert in the world, encompassing most of the southern third of the Arabian Peninsula.

The desert was supposedly the cradle of civilization on Earth, containing the ruins of Ubar, an ancient city that predates human civilizations by at least 4,000 years. As the Rub' al Khali once held the Ubari civilization, it has made locals, such as the Omani, overwhelmingly superstitious of the area. Tales of the area being cursed and forbidden to enter has propagated throughout the surrounding cultures to warn about the eldritch civilization that once existed in the area nearly ten thousand years before.

Guides were willing to take outsiders, but due to their fear of the area, they were likely to abandon those who stayed too long in the forbidden areas. This was the case for Lorenzo Cabot and his party in their expedition to find Ubar; they ignored their guide's warnings, so he fled at the first opportunity.

In Fallout Shelter Online, Lorenzo becomes interested in the Dunwich Borers mine after visiting Pickman, believing it to have something to do with the Rub' al Khali. The English script mistranslates this as "Rubal Hari Desert."

The archaeologist exam at the Pioneer Scout camp has a question that directly references the city-state. It asks "Some archaeologists think the ruins of Wilusa are a city from a famous Greek legend. Which city?" Sparta is listed as an incorrect answer to the question.

After taking control of the Whitespring bunker, Thomas Eckhart purged all those who did not wish to continue the war effort against the Chinese. This left him with only 48 members under his command, a fact he lamented with MODUS. He rallied, referencing the Battle of Thermopylae, how King Leonidas held a pass against the Persian army with his 300 Spartans, and how legendary they would become if just the 48 of them could win the war against China.

Before the Great War, Poseidon Energy was involved with every form of power production, distribution, and supply in existence. Unlike other energy moguls, they diversified and profited hugely from solar, fusion, as well as alternative power sources. They had a vast array of offices, plants, warehouses, safe houses, and other facilities across North America. One such location was a large mining facility located in the American Southwest.Fallout: The Roleplaying Game Rulebook p.232: "Poseidon Energy had offices, plants, warehouses, and even safe houses across North America. A few of the more notable in the wasteland include, but are not limited to...

Following the war the facility may have been held by a faction, remnants and descendants of the original staff, or still lie waiting to be discovered by wastelanders.

entities.name: Random encounter
entities.description:
A random encounter is a common RPG situation. It most often occurs when the player character is traversing a distance across the world map or a dungeon, resulting in a conflict with a randomly chosen opponent. In Fallout and Fallout 2, random encounters are only encountered on the world map and can be as simple as a trader wishing to show you their wares, or as convoluted as finding a tin man who needs to be oiled.

Not every encounter is hostile. Not every dangerous encounter involves aggressively minded NPCs (such as "Stampede" or "Dehydration" encounters in Fallout). Not every encounter even has an NPC on its map ("Old battle" encounter). Some random encounters are unique, and happen only once during the course of the game (or not at all) - these are commonly known as special encounters.

The kind of encounter depends on many factors. The main one is player's location on the World map. Others may be the player character's Outdoorsman skill, Karma level or reputation, as well as their previous actions during the game.

Encounters on Desert squares depend on the player's location on the world map (split into 13 areas based on towns and other landmarks). Encounters on Coast, Mountain and City squares have less categories to choose from.

entities.description:
The Belt is a region in the former midwest United States.

In 2195, one of the Brotherhood of Steel's zeppelins was lost in this region after being crushed by a great storm while crossing the western mountains. Survivors were captured by super mutants whose camp was just south of the crash site. After challenging the mutant leader Gammorin, Paladin Latham became the new leader of the super mutants. He then forged them into a powerful army, seizing control over the region.

Later in 2197, the reorganized remnants of the Brotherhood advanced into the region seeking the legendary Vault 0. Their confrontation with Gammorin's Army ended in Brotherhood's unconditional victory. The remaining super mutants were scattered and either exterminated or recruited to the Brotherhood ranks.

The Belt appears only in Fallout Tactics.

entities.description:
The Colorado Plateau is a geographic region of the American Southwest.

Grand Staircase, the region that Daniel hopes to evacuate the Sorrows to during the events of the war for Zion, is located deep within the Colorado Plateau. Joshua Graham mentions that in the Great Basin and Colorado Plateau, all tribes are known for a specific weapon, such as Dead Horses' wooden war clubs or the Sorrows' yao guai gauntlets.

The Colorado Plateau is mentioned only in the Fallout: New Vegas add-on Honest Hearts.

entities.name: Death Valley
entities.description:
Death Valley is a mentioned-only location .

Stretching across the border between the former states of California and Nevada, the so-named "Death Valley" was one of the hottest places in the world before the Great War (enough to be a point of reference for heat). Even so, this did not preclude human development in the area: Hopeville and Ashton were a pair of military cities established near the valley before the Great War, together with a network of nuclear missile silos.

Following the nuclear apocalypse, the region continued to be a lethal obstacle, together with the nearby area known as the Big Empty. The emergence of the Divide nearby shortly before the First Battle of Hoover Dam severely complicated the NCR's logistical advantage, as between the scorching heat of Death Valley, the seemingly impassable lands of the Big Empty, and the Divide's lethal storm activity, it prevented the use of California State Route 127 as a supply route and effectively wiped out all supply lines and land routes north of the Mojave Outpost, preventing the NCR from pursuing and totally destroying Caesar's Legion after the battle and giving their enemy a chance to flee back into Arizona to marshal their strength for the future Second Battle of Hoover Dam.

Death Valley is visible on the world map of and mentioned in the Vault Dweller's Survival Guide and .

entities.name: East Coast
entities.description:
The East Coast, also known as the Eastern Seaboard or Atlantic Seaboard, refers to the easternmost states of the pre-War United States of America.

The East, much like the rest of post-War America, is a lawless wasteland. The Great War did not spare it in any way, although some areas were less devastated by the war than others, and so civilization has rebuilt to varying degrees across the East. While some major centers such as Pittsburgh and Washington, D.C. were heavily bombarded by nuclear ordnance, rural areas, such as in West Virginia and parts of Maryland, were mostly spared, though still subject to mutants and radioactive fallout. Other major cities, such as Boston and Atlantic City, were less heavily targeted, but also experienced varying levels of societal collapse.

Frida Madani comments on the coastal region east of Appalachia, describing it as having been "hit a lot harder" than Appalachia and irradiated to the point that she was turned into a ghoul. Joe Creigh also comes from the coast of Virginia and made his way to Appalachia in 2103. Rucker describes traveling south along the coast along with a group of stragglers, avoiding the dangers of the wasteland in order to reach Appalachia.

Adams Air Force Base was a major United States Air Force base before the Great War. Located just outside the Capital Wasteland, the base is accessible through the presidential metro, and in 2277 served as a secondary headquarters for the Enclave, supplementing their installation at Raven Rock. Enclave operations here were centered in the mobile base crawler, which had the satellite controls needed to call down orbital strikes on several locations in the Capital Wasteland. The base was captured by the Brotherhood of Steel in 2277, following the Lone Wanderer's destruction of the mobile base crawler.

entities.name: The Island
entities.description:
The Island, formally known as Mount Desert Island, is a land body found off the coast of Maine and serves as the setting of .

In the time before the Great War, Mount Desert Island, situated off the coast of the state of Maine was home to Acadia National Park, and also hosted an experimental wind farm on the mountainside intended to serve as a "clean" alternative to nuclear power; the project was set to be shut down and dismantled at the end of October 2077 due to the threat that wind power presented to its nuclear-based parent company. The Cliff's Edge Hotel was also used as the surface structure below which Vault 118 was constructed to house its affluent residents who turned themselves into robobrains.

Following the nuclear apocalypse, the Island's landscape was permanently changed. The nuclear fallout resulted in the landscape being perpetually blanketed in a thick, radioactive fog; over 200 years of exposure has resulted in nearly every species on the Island being severely mutated while only a few areas are still habitable by humanity.

By 2287, three major factions inhabit the Island: the residents of the port town of Bar Harbor, now called Far Harbor; a local chapter of the Church of the Children of Atom operating out of a pre-War military submarine base called the Nucleus; and Acadia, a refuge inhabited by runaway synths escaping the Institute.

entities.name: New California
entities.description:
New California, also referred to as the New West, Core Region, or simply, and more commonly California, is a loosely defined territory situated on the former American West Coast and Southwest, and is one of the most detailed and fleshed-out regions in the Fallout series, being the setting for the first two entries, Fallout and Fallout 2, and further expanded upon in Fallout: New Vegas.

At the furthest point of expansion in the timeline, New California stretches from Baja in the south to Klamath in the north and is said to cover most of the pre-War American states of California, Oregon and Nevada as well as northern parts of the pre-War Mexican territory. In 2186, five independent states that previously formed in the region: Shady, Maxson, Boneyard, the Hub, and Dayglow elected to join together as a new nation called the New California Republic, giving its name to the territory and going on to become one of the largest known factions in the post-War wasteland.

The nuclear fire of the Great War affected large swaths of the United States on the West Coast. Much of the coastline was devastated, particularly around San Diego and Los Angeles. Massive craters were created as a result of the bombardment, the largest one situated where Orange County used to be located.

The scale of the attack was not without reason, however. Before the War, many important facilities were located in the region. One such example was a West-Tek Research Facility, established in 2055 to research the New Plague (later becoming the birthplace of the Forced Evolutionary Virus). Other vital installations include the Mariposa Military Base (newly constructed as of January 2077) and the Sierra Army Depot (in operation since 1942, refitted in 2050 as a top-secret research base, and then converted in 2077 into an automated defense base).

entities.name: Point Lookout
entities.description:
Point Lookout is a swamp wasteland and region in the former state of Maryland in 2277. It is downriver from the Capital Wasteland.

Long before the Great War, the region of Point Lookout was discovered by English explorer John Smith in 1612. Over two decades later, in 1634, two ships known as the "Ark" and the "Dove" landed near Point Lookout. The settlers constructed the Ark & Dove Cathedral, naming it after the vessels that brought them to the New World. Point Lookout continued as a successful settlement.

During the American Civil War, Point Lookout served as the site of significant military activity, and the Lone Wanderer can still find Confederate hats throughout the region. The small seaside town, "Pilgrim's Landing." became a tourist attraction, particularly with the boardwalk that pays homage to those original English settlers.

As during the American Civil War, the secluded backwater swamps of Point Lookout harbored another military prison, the Turtledove Detention Camp, for Chinese-Americans suspected of espionage against the United States during the Sino-American War. The infamous spy Wan Yang was arrested in Point Lookout and taken there for interrogation, subsequently perishing at the camp. Meanwhile, just off the coast of Point Lookout, a Chinese submarine patrolled the waters gathering information. This submarine was ultimately discovered and disabled, at which point a single surviving submariner was captured and taken to Turtledove. The United States Navy successfully salvaged the submarine just prior to the Great War.

entities.name: Zion Canyon
entities.description:
Zion Canyon, also known as Zion Valley and formerly known as Zion National Park, is a pre-War natural landmark in the former American state of Utah. It serves as the setting for .

Being located far to the north of the Mojave Desert (around a week when hiking on-foot) and remote from most hubs of civilization, Zion was spared the devastation of direct attack by nuclear weapons on the day of the Great War. However even then, it was not safe from the resulting fallout, eventually leading to most of its waters becoming heavily irradiated and much of its plant and wild life to die off. But that was not the end for Zion, as due to its natural qualities such as wind currents frequently blowing through the canyon, in only a few weeks' time, much of the radiation had disappeared, allowing for both flora and fauna, though mutated by the radiation, to return and for Zion to regain its natural splendor, albeit slowly.

Though its status as a national park was rendered defunct by the dissolution of America after the Great War, Zion still entreated visitors, the first post-War of which was Randall Clark, a former US soldier that had narrowly escaped the destruction of his hometown of Salt Lake City, though his wife and son were not so fortunate. Constructing campsites around the various natural caves dotting the canyon over his years-long residence in Zion, Clark focused solely on survival while keeping a journal to record his thoughts and his experiences living in the post-War wasteland.

In 2095, Zion received more visitors in the form of a group of Spanish-speaking refugees that had supposedly traveled all the way north from Mexico. Still living in the canyon, Clark watched over them while remaining unseen, helping them in secret such as giving antibiotics when one of their members was injured. However, when the canyon's next visitors came, circumstances became worse as a 118-strong, armed group of former Vault dwellers from Vault 22 attacked and killed most of the Mexican refugees, taking some prisoner only to later consume them. All of this was witnessed by Clark, who swore vengeance on the Vault dwellers and instigated a guerilla war against them, lasting 10 months and by the end of it, he had managed to kill 80 of their original 118, causing the survivors to flee from Zion. However, Clark was not alone in the canyon as he later discovered a woman named Sylvie that had escaped from the Vault dwellers. After nursing her back to health, the two grew closer, becoming romantic and around 2100, Sylvie became pregnant with a son. But when she went into labor, the baby ended up being a breech birth and didn't survive, and when Clark attempted to sedate Sylvie to surgically save the child, she didn't wake up. After burying his second family, Clark was left alone in the canyon once more.
